ProgramName: Bachelor of Business Administration in Accounting
Requirements: Admission to the Bachelor of Business Administration (BBA) in Accounting program is available through two main paths: Direct Entry for high school seniors and a current student application for those already enrolled at UW-Madison. Requirements include a completed application (Common App for freshmen), official high school or college transcripts, a personal essay, and a one-page resume. For current UW-Madison students, specific prerequisite coursework such as calculus and communication skills must be completed or in progress. The admissions process is holistic, evaluating academic excellence, leadership, and extracurricular involvement. ACT/SAT scores are currently optional.
Description: Accountants provide the information that is necessary for people to make good decisions. Because this is true in all types of organizations, accounting is often called the 'language of business.' Accounting is a great major for students who are interested in how businesses work, who enjoy working with numbers, and who want to pursue a career that offers a wide range of opportunities. The curriculum is designed to provide students with the knowledge and skills they need to pursue a variety of career paths, including public accounting, corporate accounting, government, and nonprofit organizations.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).
Accredidation: The Wisconsin School of Business is accredited by AACSB International (the Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business). The accounting program also holds specialized accounting accreditation from AACSB.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Business Administration in Actuarial Science
Requirements: Admission to the BBA in Actuarial Science program at the Wisconsin School of Business occurs through two pathways: Direct Admission for incoming freshmen and the Pre-Business application for current UW-Madison or transfer students. The application process involves a holistic review that considers academic performance, leadership, and involvement. For the Pre-Business application, students must complete specific prerequisite courses (including Communication Part A, Psychology, and Calculus) and submit a one-page resume and a 500-word essay. Actuarial Science majors are specifically required to take MATH 221 or equivalent as a prerequisite for the major-specific coursework.
Description: Actuarial science is the study of the evaluation and measurement of risk. The actuarial science program at UW–Madison consistently ranks as one of the best in the nation. It has been recognized by the Society of Actuaries as a Center of Actuarial Excellence. Actuaries use mathematical and statistical skills to solve relevant business problems. They evaluate the likelihood of future events—such as death, disability, or property loss—and design creative ways to reduce the impact of these risks. The curriculum provides students with the mathematical, statistical, and business skills needed to analyze financial risks and solve complex problems in insurance, pensions, and other financial areas, and helps prepare students for the professional examinations required to become a certified actuary.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).
Accredidation: Recognized by the Society of Actuaries as a Center of Actuarial Excellence (CAE).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in African American Studies
Requirements: There are no requirements for students to declare the African American Studies major. All undergraduate students are eligible to declare African American Studies. To declare, students should schedule an appointment with the undergraduate advisor.
Description: The Department of African American Studies offers a multidisciplinary curriculum that examines the history, culture, and experiences of people of African descent in the United States, the Caribbean, and the broader African Diaspora. Our faculty and students engage in critical inquiry into the social, political, and cultural forces that have shaped the lives of African Americans and other members of the African Diaspora. The department’s program of study is designed to provide students with a comprehensive understanding of the African American experience through several disciplinary lenses, including history, literature, art, sociology, and political science. Students in the program develop skills in critical thinking, research, and communication that are essential for a wide range of careers, including education, law, public policy, and the arts. Our curriculum also prepares students for graduate study in a variety of fields.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://guide.wisc.edu/undergraduate/letters-science/african-american-studies/african-american-studies-ba/

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in African American Studies
Requirements: To declare the African American Studies major, students should meet with the undergraduate advisor. All students are welcome to declare the major. General university admission for freshmen requires the submission of a completed application (Common App or UW System App), two required essays, official high school transcripts, and an optional letter of recommendation. The university is currently test-optional through the summer 2027 term.
Description: The Department of African American Studies is an intellectual community committed to producing, refining and helping students to master a body of knowledge about African American life. For over 40 years, the department has offered a multidisciplinary curriculum in which students and faculty examine the history, culture, society, and political organization of African Americans and other peoples of African descent. Drawing on the humanities and the social sciences, the department offers a varied program of study that leads to the Bachelor of Arts or Bachelor of Science degree.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in African Cultural Studies
Requirements: Students are eligible to declare the African Cultural Studies major if they have a 2.000 cumulative GPA. To declare, students should meet with the department's undergraduate advisor.
Description: The Department of African Cultural Studies provides research and teaching in the languages and expressive cultures of Africa and the African diaspora. This includes everything from Swahili and Wolof to African movies, modern African literature, and hip-hop. Our faculty and students study the connections between the different regions of the continent, and the ways that African people and their cultures have been influenced by and have influenced the rest of the world. The major provides a broad introduction to the African continent through a program of study that includes a range of courses in African languages, expressive cultures (literature, film, music, etc.), and other areas of African studies. It is especially suited for students with a wide range of interests who may wish to design an individual program of study with a particular focus or for students who wish to double-major in another field. The major also provides a solid foundation for those who plan to pursue graduate work in the humanities and social sciences, or a career in such fields as education, public health, international development, government, or international business.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://guide.wisc.edu/undergraduate/letters-science/african-cultural-studies/african-cultural-studies-ba/

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in African Cultural Studies
Requirements: To apply for admission to the University of Wisconsin–Madison as an undergraduate, applicants must submit the Common Application, which includes two required essays, an application fee, and official high school transcripts. Providing ACT or SAT scores is optional for students applying through the spring 2025 term. For the specific Bachelor of Science in African Cultural Studies major, students already enrolled at UW-Madison may declare the major at any time by meeting with the department's undergraduate advisor.
Description: The Department of African Cultural Studies focuses on the languages and expressive cultures of Africa and the African diaspora. This includes the study of languages, literatures, and other forms of cultural expression such as film, music, and performance. Our mission is to research and teach these expressive cultures in their local and global contexts. By fostering a deeper understanding of African-descended people’s historical and contemporary experiences, we aim to prepare students to engage critically and empathetically with the diverse and interconnected world in which we live. The department offers a major and a minor. Our courses provide an multidisciplinary and international perspective on the histories and contemporary experiences of people in and from Africa. We offer three or more years of study in Arabic, Hausa, Swahili, Wolof, Yoruba, and Zulu. Our curriculum also includes courses in literature, film, music, and other cultural forms.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, Need-based, Departmental (e.g., Bauman Family Scholarship)

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Agricultural and Applied Economics
Requirements: To declare the Agricultural and Applied Economics major, a student must be a current UW–Madison student. General undergraduate admission to the University of Wisconsin-Madison involves a holistic review process that considers academic performance (high school grades and rigor of coursework), personal essays, extracurricular activities, and letters of recommendation. ACT or SAT scores are currently optional for applicants.
Department: College of Agricultural and Life Sciences
Concentration: Food and Agriculture, Environmental and Resource Economics, and International and Community Development
Description: How can we address the problem of world hunger? How can we reduce pollution? How do changes in the food system affect the well-being of farmers and consumers? Why are some countries rich while others remain poor? These are the kinds of questions students in the Agricultural and Applied Economics (AAE) major learn to answer. Using economic principles and data, students study food and fiber production, consumption and trade, environmental and natural resource management, and international and community development. This major provides a solid foundation in economic theory and math, as well as the data science and communication skills used by professional economists. Our students can choose from three concentrations: Food and Agriculture, Environmental and Resource Economics, and International and Community Development.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Agricultural Business Management
Requirements: Undergraduate students who wish to declare the Agricultural Business Management major must be admitted to UW–Madison and the College of Agricultural and Life Sciences (CALS). There are no additional requirements for admission to this major. For information about university-wide admission, please see the Office of Admissions and Recruitment website.
Department: College of Agricultural and Life Sciences
Description: Students in the agricultural business management (ABM) major learn how to manage companies that produce and market food and fiber. The major is designed for students who want to become leaders in business, specifically the business of agriculture. It is one of two majors offered by the Department of Agricultural and Applied Economics. The ABM major integrates the study of economics, finance, marketing, and management with the study of agricultural systems. Students learn to apply economic principles and business management tools to the challenges of feeding and clothing a growing world population. Graduates from the program find employment in a wide range of industries including food manufacturing, commodity trading, finance and banking, farm management, and marketing. In the ABM program, students are encouraged to pursue an internship, and many students take advantage of study abroad opportunities. The major has a relatively small number of students, and there is an active student organization—the UW–Madison NAMA (National Agri-Marketing Association) chapter—that provides professional development and networking opportunities. The ABM major is also well-suited for students who plan to continue their education in graduate school or law school.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://guide.wisc.edu/undergraduate/agricultural-life-sciences/agricultural-applied-economics/agricultural-business-management-bs/

Requirements: Admission to the Bachelor of Science in Agronomy involves a holistic review process. Applicants must submit a completed application (Common Application or UW System Application), official high school transcripts, two required essays, and one letter of recommendation. Students are expected to have completed a rigorous high school curriculum including 4 units of English, 4 units of Mathematics, 3 units of Science, 3 units of Social Studies, and 2 units of a single World Language. The university is currently test-optional through 2027.
Department: College of Agricultural and Life Sciences
Description: Agronomy is the science of food and fiber production. It is a profession that manages the land to produce food, feed, fuel and fiber for a growing population while protecting the environment. Agronomists work to develop and apply sustainable ways to grow crops, improve the genetics of plants, manage weeds and pests, and maintain healthy soils. The Agronomy major provides students with a strong foundation in the biological and physical sciences, as well as practical experience in crop production and management. Students learn about plant physiology, genetics, soil science, pest management, and the economic and environmental aspects of agriculture. The curriculum is designed to prepare students for careers in a wide range of fields, including crop consulting, seed and chemical sales, farm management, research and development, and environmental conservation. Students also have the opportunity to participate in internships, research projects, and study abroad programs to gain hands-on experience and a global perspective on agriculture.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Animal Sciences
Requirements: To apply to this major, students must be admitted to the University of Wisconsin–Madison and the College of Agricultural and Life Sciences (CALS). For information about undergraduate admissions at UW–Madison, please see the Office of Admissions and Recruitment website. To declare this major, students must meet with an advisor.
Department: College of Agricultural and Life Sciences
Concentration: Animal Biology option; Production and Management option
Description: Animal sciences is the study of the biology, care, and management of animals. This includes the study of animal breeding and genetics, meat science and muscle biology, nutrition, physiology, and more. The Animal Sciences major is designed to provide students with a fundamental understanding of the biological sciences and their application to the care and management of animals. The program offers two options for students: the Animal Biology option and the Production and Management option. The Animal Biology option is designed for students interested in careers in veterinary medicine, medicine, research, or other professional fields. The Production and Management option is designed for students interested in careers in the animal industries, such as production, management, sales, or marketing.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://guide.wisc.edu/undergraduate/agricultural-life-sciences/animal-dairy-sciences/animal-sciences-bs/animal-sciences-bs_howtogetintext.pdf

Requirements: Prospective students must apply for undergraduate admission to the University of Wisconsin–Madison. The application process requires the submission of the Common Application or UW System Application, official high school transcripts, a counselor or teacher recommendation, and two required essays. For the Anthropology major specifically, students must complete at least 30 credits in Anthropology, maintain a minimum 2.000 GPA in all major courses, and complete at least 15 upper-level credits in the major in residence. The university is currently test-optional through the Spring 2027 term.
Description: Anthropology is the study of humans, past and present. To understand the full sweep and complexity of cultures across all of human history, anthropology draws and builds upon knowledge from the social and biological sciences as well as the humanities and physical sciences. A central concern of anthropologists is the application of knowledge to the solution of human problems. Historically, anthropologists in the United States have been trained in one of four areas: sociocultural anthropology, biological/physical anthropology, archaeology, and linguistics. Anthropologists often integrate the perspectives of several of these areas into their research, teaching, and professional lives.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

Requirements: To apply for the Bachelor of Science in Anthropology, applicants must complete the Common Application or the UW System Application. Required materials include official high school transcripts, two essays, and an application fee. One letter of recommendation is optional but encouraged. While ACT or SAT scores are not required for the 2024–2025 application cycle, students may choose to submit them as optional materials. Once admitted to the University, students can declare the Anthropology major at any time by meeting with the department’s undergraduate advisor.
Description: Anthropology is the study of humans, past and present. To understand the full sweep and complexity of cultures across all of human history, anthropology draws and builds upon knowledge from the social and biological sciences as well as the humanities and physical sciences. A central concern of anthropologists is the application of knowledge to the solution of human problems. Historically, anthropologists in the United States have been trained in one of four areas: sociocultural anthropology, biological/physical anthropology, archaeology, and linguistics. Anthropology majors at UW–Madison complete coursework in each of these four subfields.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Applied Mathematics, Engineering and Physics
Requirements: To declare the Applied Mathematics, Engineering, and Physics (AMEP) major, a student must have completed the first two semesters of the AMEP math sequence (currently MATH 221 and MATH 222) and the first two semesters of the AMEP physics sequence (currently PHYSICS 247 and PHYSICS 248). A student must also meet with the AMEP faculty advisor to discuss the requirements and expectations of the program.
Description: Applied Mathematics, Engineering, and Physics (AMEP) is an interdisciplinary bachelor of science degree program focusing on mathematics, physics, and engineering. It is designed for students who are interested in the application of mathematics to physical problems and who want to combine a strong background in mathematics and physics with a concentration in an area of engineering. The program is offered through the Department of Mathematics in the College of Letters & Science. Students in the program must satisfy the requirements of the College of Letters & Science that are not specific to the AMEP program (see the Requirements tab). Students in AMEP take about 20–21 credits of mathematics, about 17 credits of physics, and 12 credits of engineering. The program is excellent preparation for graduate study in any of the three areas and also provides a strong background for work in industry. A leadership committee composed of faculty from the mathematics, physics, and engineering departments oversees the program. Each student is assigned an AMEP advisor from one of the participating departments upon entering the program.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://guide.wisc.edu/undergraduate/letters-science/mathematics/applied-mathematics-engineering-physics-bs-amep/applied-mathematics-engineering-physics-bs-amep.pdf

ProgramName: Bachelor of Liberal Studies in Applied Social Science
Requirements: Admission to the Bachelor of Liberal Studies (BLS) is through the Office of Admissions and Recruitment. The program is designed for students who are not living in the Madison area and wish to complete their degree online.
Description: Applied Social Science is a 100% online program designed for adults and other students who have already earned some college credit and want to finish their degree. The Applied Social Science major provides a strong foundation in the social sciences, including sociology, psychology, and economics, while also developing the critical thinking, communication, and analytical skills needed for success in a variety of careers. Students will learn to understand and analyze complex social problems, evaluate evidence and arguments, and communicate effectively with diverse audiences. They will also gain experience in applying social science perspectives to real-world issues.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://guide.wisc.edu/undergraduate/undergraduate.pdf
ScholarshipType: Merit-based and Need-based (e.g., Success in Online Learning Scholarship, Osher Reentry Scholarship)

Requirements: New freshmen and off-campus transfer students are admitted directly to the Art program. All applicants must meet the general admission requirements of the University of Wisconsin–Madison. Students may also be admitted to the Art program after they have enrolled at UW–Madison. Requirements for admission through the on-campus application are: Complete ART 102, ART 104, ART 107, ART 108, and ART 212; Earn a 2.50 cumulative GPA on the UW–Madison campus. The Art Department does not require a portfolio for admission to the Art–BS or Art–BFA programs.
Description: The Art Department’s undergraduate programs provide a rigorous environment for the physical, intellectual, and creative development of students. Its goal is to provide a strong foundation for a variety of careers in the visual arts, but the faculty also recognizes that a degree in the visual arts may be used as a foundation for other professional careers. In keeping with the university’s dedication to research and teaching, the department is committed to the development of the individual student as a creative artist and an informed citizen of the visual world. The Bachelor of Science (BS)–Art degree is a liberal arts degree with a major in art. It is designed for students who want a strong education in the visual arts within the context of a broad program of general studies. (This is distinct from the Bachelor of Fine Arts degree, which is a professional degree.) The BS–Art degree may be completed with or without an emphasis in graphic design. Students who want a strong foundation for a teaching career in the visual arts should consider the BS–Art Education degree.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://guide.wisc.edu/undergraduate/education/art/art-bs/art-bs.pdf
Accredidation: UW–Madison is accredited by the Higher Learning Commission (HLC). The Department of Art is also an accredited institutional member of the National Association of Schools of Art and Design (NASAD).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Fine Arts in Art
Requirements: Prospective Art–BFA students should admit to UW–Madison as Art–BS students. All students, including those who are already at UW–Madison, those who are transferring from another institution, and those who are applying as a second undergraduate degree candidate, must be admitted to UW–Madison to be considered for admission to the School of Education. Students may be admitted to the Art–BFA degree program by the School of Education after completing the Art–BS degree requirements or its equivalent (30 total credits, including 15 credits of studio art and 6 credits of art history) and having a 2.50 cumulative GPA (on a 4.00 scale) on all college-level coursework. These requirements are minimums and are not a guarantee of admission. Students must submit a portfolio for review by the Art Department to be admitted to the BFA degree program.
Description: The Department of Art offers two undergraduate degree options: the Bachelor of Science in Art (BS–Art) and the Bachelor of Fine Arts in Art (BFA). Both programs provide students with a solid foundation in the visual arts and the opportunity for in-depth study in one or more areas of studio art. The BFA is a professional degree that requires a higher concentration of studio and art history credits. It is intended for students who are interested in pursuing a career as a professional artist or who plan to apply to graduate school (Master of Fine Arts). Students in the BFA program develop a deep and specialized knowledge of art and design through intensive studio work. They have the opportunity to focus their studies in various areas, including ceramics, glass, graphic design, painting and drawing, photography, printmaking, sculpture, and video/performance/installation.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://guide.wisc.edu/undergraduate/education/art/art-bfa/art-bfa.pdf
Accredidation: The Department of Art is an accredited institutional member of the National Association of Schools of Art and Design (NASAD).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Art History
Requirements: Students must apply for admission to the University of Wisconsin–Madison through the Office of Admissions and Recruitment. There are no additional admission requirements for the Art History major; students may declare the major at any time. General university application requirements include a completed application (Common App or UW System Application), two required essays, high school transcripts, and an application fee. A letter of recommendation is optional but encouraged. For the 2024-2025 application cycles, submission of ACT or SAT scores is optional.
Description: The Department of Art History covers the global history of art, architecture, and visual culture from antiquity to the present. We offer a wide range of courses that explore the production, circulation, and consumption of images and objects across different cultures and time periods. Our program is designed to provide students with a broad and deep knowledge of the visual arts, while also developing their skills in critical thinking, research, and writing. Students learn to analyze works of art in their historical, social, and cultural contexts, and to understand the ways in which art has shaped and been shaped by human experience. Art History majors are prepared for a variety of careers in museums, galleries, auction houses, arts administration, education, and many other fields.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://bulletins.psu.edu/undergraduate/colleges/arts-architecture/art-history-ba/

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Art History
Requirements: To apply for undergraduate admission to the University of Wisconsin–Madison, including the Bachelor of Science in Art History, applicants must submit the following: a completed application (Common App or UW System application), two required essays, official high school transcripts, and one letter of recommendation. For the major specifically, any student in good standing may declare the major at any time by meeting with the undergraduate advisor.
Description: Art history is the study of the visual arts—painting, sculpture, architecture, and other media—in their historical and cultural contexts. The major in Art History is designed to give students a broad knowledge of the history of art in various parts of the world. It also provides an introduction to the methodologies of the discipline and the opportunity for more intensive study of specific periods and topics. In addition to preparing students for graduate study in art history and related fields, the major provides a strong foundation for careers in museums, galleries, auction houses, and other arts organizations.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

Requirements: To be admitted to the University of Wisconsin–Madison, applicants must submit either the Common Application or the Universities of Wisconsin Application. Standard requirements include two essays, official high school transcripts, and one letter of recommendation (up to two are accepted). For the application cycles through Summer 2027, UW–Madison is test-optional, meaning ACT and SAT scores are not required. The Astronomy-Physics major itself is open to all undergraduate students at UW–Madison, and students typically declare the major after completing introductory coursework.
Description:
The astronomy–physics major provides a solid foundation in both physics and astronomy. It is recommended for students who plan to pursue graduate study in astronomy or astrophysics, or who wish to work in a related field. The major is offered through the Department of Astronomy and the Department of Physics.

The Department of Astronomy also offers a major in Astronomy (http://guide.wisc.edu/undergraduate/letters-science/astronomy/astronomy-ba-bs/). The Astronomy–Physics major requires more math and physics than the Astronomy major. The Physics department offers a major in Physics (http://guide.wisc.edu/undergraduate/letters-science/physics/physics-ba-bs/). The Astronomy–Physics major requires more astronomy than the Physics major.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

Requirements: Admission to the Bachelor of Science in Astronomy-Physics begins with the general undergraduate application to the University of Wisconsin-Madison. Required application materials include high school transcripts, two application essays, and one letter of recommendation (optional). UW-Madison is test-optional through the Summer 2027 term. Once admitted to the university, students must complete specific prerequisite coursework, including calculus (MATH 221 and 222) and introductory physics (PHYSICS 247, 248, 249 or equivalent), to officially declare the major.
Description: The astronomy–physics major is designed for students who want a rigorous performance-based program in astronomy and physics. It is intended for students who wish to pursue graduate study in astronomy, physics, or a related field. The major provides a strong foundation in both astronomy and physics, with a focus on understanding the physical universe. Students in the program take a series of physics and mathematics courses as well as courses in astronomy. The major is administered by the Department of Astronomy.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Atmospheric and Oceanic Sciences
Requirements: The University of Wisconsin–Madison uses a holistic review process for all freshman applicants. To be considered for admission, students must submit a completed application (Common App or UW System App) which includes: official high school transcripts, two required essays, and a list of extracurricular activities, honors, and awards. High school coursework requirements include 4 units of English, 4 units of Mathematics, 3-4 units of Social Studies, 3-4 units of Science, and 2 units of a single World Language. Submission of standardized test scores (ACT or SAT) is optional for applicants through the spring 2025 term. One letter of recommendation is optional but encouraged.
Description: Atmospheric and oceanic sciences (AOS) is a field of study that focuses on the physics and chemistry of the Earth’s atmosphere and oceans. The AOS major provides students with a broad background in the study of the atmosphere and oceans, and the processes that drive their behavior. Students learn about weather systems, climate change, ocean currents, and the interactions between the atmosphere and the oceans. The AOS major is designed to prepare students for a variety of careers in atmospheric and oceanic sciences, including weather forecasting, climate analysis, oceanography, and environmental consulting. The major also provides a strong foundation for graduate study in AOS or related fields. The department offers two undergraduate majors: the atmospheric and oceanic sciences major (leading to a bachelor of science degree) and the atmospheric and oceanic sciences major (leading to a bachelor of arts degree). The requirements for the two majors are identical, except for the college-level requirements for the BA and BS degrees.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Atmospheric and Oceanic Sciences
Requirements: Prospective students apply through the general University of Wisconsin–Madison Office of Admissions and Recruitment. Requirements include high school transcripts, two essays (one focusing on why the applicant is interested in their selected major), at least one letter of recommendation, and an application fee. For the 2024-2025 and 2025-2026 application cycles, providing ACT or SAT scores is optional. There are no specific prerequisite requirements for declaring the Atmospheric and Oceanic Sciences major beyond being admitted to the University.
Description: The atmospheric and oceanic sciences (AOS) describe the behavior of the atmosphere and oceans and their role in the Earth system. The AOS undergraduate major provides students with a high-quality, broad-based education in the atmospheric and oceanic sciences. The program's goals are to provide students with an understanding of the physics and dynamics of the atmosphere and oceans, to prepare students for a variety of careers in the atmospheric and oceanic sciences, and to provide students with a strong foundation for graduate study. Preparation for a professional career in the atmospheric and oceanic sciences—including the National Weather Service, private industry, and research organizations—is the primary goal of the undergraduate program. Students learn about the fundamental principles of physics, chemistry, and mathematics as they apply to the atmosphere and oceans. The program is also designed to provide students with a solid foundation for graduate study in the atmospheric and oceanic sciences or related fields.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

Requirements: To apply for admission to the University of Wisconsin–Madison, applicants must submit the following: a completed application (Common Application or the University of Wisconsin System Application), two required essays, official high school transcripts, and an application fee. Admission is based on a holistic review process that considers academic excellence (GPA, rigor of coursework), personal characteristics, and involvement. Standardized test scores (ACT or SAT) are optional for the 2024–25 and 2025–26 terms. Students must also meet the minimum high school course requirements (English, Math, Social Science, Science, and World Language).
Description: Biochemistry is the study of the chemical processes that occur within living organisms. It is a broad and fascinating field that encompasses everything from the structure and function of proteins and DNA to the metabolism of cells and the regulation of gene expression. Biochemistry is essential for understanding how life works, and it has many important applications in medicine, agriculture, and biotechnology. The biochemistry major provides a strong foundation in the chemical and biological sciences. Students take courses in chemistry, physics, mathematics, and biology, as well as specialized courses in biochemistry. The major also provides opportunities for students to participate in research, which is a great way to gain hands-on experience and learn about the latest discoveries in the field. Students who graduate with a degree in biochemistry are well-prepared for a variety of careers in science, medicine, and other fields.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).
Accredidation: The University of Wisconsin–Madison’s undergraduate biochemistry program is accredited by the American Society for Biochemistry and Molecular Biology (ASBMB).

Requirements: To apply for freshman admission to the Bachelor of Science in Biochemistry program, applicants must submit: a completed application (Common Application), two required essays, official high school transcripts, an application fee, and an optional letter of recommendation. UW–Madison is test-optional for all applicants; you may choose to submit ACT or SAT scores, but they are not required.
Department: College of Agricultural and Life Sciences; College of Letters & Science
Description: Biochemistry is the study of the chemical processes within and relating to living organisms. It is a laboratory-based science that combines biology and chemistry. By using chemical knowledge and techniques, biochemists can understand and solve biological problems. Biochemistry focuses on what’s happening inside our cells, studying components like proteins, lipids, and organelles. It also looks at how cells communicate with each other, for example, during growth or fighting illness. Biochemists need to understand how the structure of a molecule relates to its function, allowing them to predict how molecules will interact. Biochemistry covers a range of scientific disciplines, including genetics, microbiology, forensics, plant science, and medicine. Because of its breadth, biochemistry is very important and advances in this field of science over the past 100 years have been staggering. It’s a very exciting time to be part of this fascinating area of study.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).
Accredidation: The UW–Madison Biochemistry undergraduate program is accredited by the American Society for Biochemistry and Molecular Biology (ASBMB).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Biological Systems Engineering
Requirements: Admission to the Bachelor of Science in Biological Systems Engineering is handled through the general University of Wisconsin-Madison undergraduate admissions process. Requirements include the submission of either the Common Application or the UW System Application, official high school transcripts, and a report of extracurricular activities and work experience. Applicants must have completed specific high school coursework (including 4 units of English, 4 units of Math, 3 units of Social Studies, 3 units of Science, and 2 units of a Single Foreign Language). Two essays are required as part of the application. The university follows a holistic review process that considers academic performance, course rigor, leadership, and community involvement.
Department: College of Agricultural and Life Sciences
Concentration: Food and Bioprocess Engineering, Machinery Systems Engineering, Natural Resources and Environmental Engineering
Description: Biological Systems Engineering (BSE) is an engineering major that uses the sciences of biology, chemistry, and physics, along with engineering mathematics and computer-aided design to solve problems in biological systems. BSE is a broad field, and UW–Madison’s BSE program allows students to focus their studies on one of three areas: food and bioprocess engineering, machinery systems engineering, or natural resources and environmental engineering. Students who graduate from the program work in many different industries, from designing equipment for the next generation of off-road vehicles to discovering new ways to process food for a growing population to developing ways to protect the environment and provide clean water for everyone. Graduates are ready for careers in industry and consulting, and are prepared for graduate school and professional programs in medicine and law.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).
Accredidation: Accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org, under the General Criteria and the Program Criteria for Biological and Similarly Named Engineering Programs.

Requirements: All students interested in the Biology major must first be admitted to UW–Madison. Students can then declare the major. For more information about the major, including how to declare, please see the major website.
Description: Biology is the study of life. The biology major is designed for students with broad interests in the biological sciences. It is intended primarily for students who are interested in a variety of organisms (from bacteria to plants to animals) and for those who wish to explore the various levels of biological organization (from molecules to cells to organisms to ecosystems). The biology major provides students with a broad foundation in the biological sciences, with the opportunity for students to specialize in a particular area through the selection of elective courses. The biology major is a collaborative program between the College of Agricultural and Life Sciences (CALS) and the College of Letters & Science (L&S). Students may complete the major through either college, based on their individual interests and goals.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://guide.wisc.edu/undergraduate/letters-science/integrative-biology/biology-ba/

Requirements: To be considered for admission to the Bachelor of Science in Biology program, applicants must submit a complete application including: official high school transcripts, two required essays, and one letter of recommendation (optional). Applicants are expected to have completed a minimum of 17 high school units, including 4 units of English, 4 units of Mathematics, 3 units of Social Science, 3 units of Natural Science, and 2 units of a single foreign language. UW–Madison is currently test-optional; students may choose whether to submit ACT or SAT scores.
Department: College of Letters & Science and College of Agricultural and Life Sciences
Description: The biology major is a popular choice for students who want a broad background in the biological sciences. It provides students with a strong foundation in the concepts and principles of biology, from the molecular level to the ecosystem level. Students in the biology major have the opportunity to participate in research and to tailor their coursework to their interests and career goals. The biology major is a good choice for students who are interested in careers in medicine, dentistry, veterinary medicine, research, teaching, and many other fields. The biology major is an intercollege major. Students may choose to be in either the College of Agricultural and Life Sciences (CALS) or the College of Letters & Science (L&S). Both colleges offer the same biology major requirements.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Biomedical Engineering
Requirements: To apply for the Bachelor of Science in Biomedical Engineering, freshman applicants must submit the Common Application or the UW System Application. Application requirements include the completion of two essays (a personal statement and a why UW-Madison essay), official high school transcripts, and one letter of recommendation (optional). Standardized test scores (ACT/SAT) are optional for applicants through the Spring 2025 term. Admission is competitive and based on academic record, including the rigor of the high school curriculum, as well as non-academic factors such as leadership, community service, and extracurricular activities.
Concentration: Bioinstrumentation and Medical Devices; Biomedical Imaging and Optics; Biomaterials, Cellular, and Tissue Engineering; Biomechanics; Systems and Synthetic Biology
Description: Biomedical engineering (BME) is the application of engineering tools and methods to solve problems in biology and medicine. It is a field of great breadth, with areas of focus that include: Bioinstrumentation: using electronics, microcomputers and sensors to design instruments for medical diagnosis and treatment. Biomaterials, Cellular and Tissue Engineering: developing materials and methods to repair or replace damaged or diseased organs and tissues. Biomechanics: applying mechanical engineering principles to biological systems to understand their function and to design medical devices. Biomedical Imaging and Optics: applying the physics of light and sound to the development of new techniques for imaging and visualizing the human body and biological processes. Systems and Synthetic Biology: applying engineering principles to the study of complex biological systems to understand and predict their behavior, and to design new biological parts and systems. The Biomedical Engineering program at UW–Madison offers an undergraduate curriculum that provides students with a strong foundation in both engineering and the life sciences. Students in the program have the opportunity to participate in research with world-class faculty and to gain practical experience through internships and co-op programs.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).
Accredidation: The Bachelor of Science in Biomedical Engineering at the University of Wisconsin–Madison is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org, under the commission’s General Program Criteria and the Program Criteria for Bioengineering and Biomedical and Similarly Named Engineering Programs.

Requirements: There are no additional admission requirements for the major. Students are encouraged to declare as soon as they have decided on the major. Students should meet with the undergraduate advisor to declare the major.
Description: Plants are the foundation of life on earth. They provide us with oxygen, food, medicine, and fuel. They also play a critical role in regulating the Earth’s climate and supporting biodiversity. Botany is the study of plants, including their structure, function, growth, reproduction, metabolism, development, diseases, and chemical properties and evolutionary relationships among different groups. The Botany major at UW–Madison provides students with a strong foundation in the plant sciences. The program offers a wide range of courses, from introductory biology to advanced topics such as plant physiology, plant anatomy, plant ecology, and plant evolution. Students also have the opportunity to participate in research with faculty members who are leaders in their fields.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://guide.wisc.edu/undergraduate/letters-science/botany/botany-ba/

Requirements: Students may declare the botany major at any time. To complete the major, a student must complete at least 30 credits in botany courses or courses in other departments that are approved for the Botany major. In addition to the credits for the major, students must complete requirements for the B.A. or B.S. degree in the College of Letters & Science and fulfill the University General Education Requirements.
Description: Botany is the study of plants, algae, and fungi. These organisms are the essential foundation of life on Earth. They produce the oxygen we breathe, the food we eat, and the fuel and fiber we use. They also create the habitats that support the world's biodiversity. The study of botany is critical to understanding how ecosystems function, how we can protect biodiversity, and how we can develop sustainable ways to produce food, fuel, and other resources. The botany major provides students with a broad background in the biology of plants, from the molecular level to the ecosystem level. Students in the major take courses in plant anatomy, physiology, ecology, evolution and systematics. They also have the opportunity to participate in research with faculty members in the Department of Botany. The major is designed to prepare students for a wide range of careers in areas such as research, education, conservation, and industry.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://guide.wisc.edu/undergraduate/letters-science/botany/botany.pdf

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Cartography and Geographic Information Systems
Requirements: Students may declare the Cartography and Geographic Information Systems major at any time. To declare, students should meet with a cartography and GIS advisor.
Description:
Geography is a broad-based discipline that explores the relationships between people and their environments. Geography is a science that is both social and natural—it examines people and their societies and the natural environment in which they exist. Geographers study the interaction between these two systems and how they vary across space.

The department also offers a major in cartography and geographic information systems (GIS).

Cartography and GIS is a major that focuses on the design, development, and use of maps and geospatial technologies. Students learn how to collect, analyze, and visualize spatial data to solve problems in a wide range of fields, including environmental management, urban planning, public health, and business. The major provides students with a strong foundation in the theoretical and practical aspects of cartography, GIS, and remote sensing. Students also have the opportunity to take courses in related fields such as geography, computer science, and statistics.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://guide.wisc.edu/undergraduate/letters-science/geography/geography-ba/

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Cartography and Geographic Information Systems
Requirements: Students may declare the Cartography and Geographic Information Systems major at any time. To declare, students should visit the department’s website and schedule an appointment with the undergraduate advisor.
Description: The Cartography and Geographic Information Systems (GIS) major focuses on the design, compilation, and production of maps and the management, analysis, and display of spatial data. Students in this major gain a strong foundation in cartography, GIS, and remote sensing, as well as the technical and analytical skills needed to work in a variety of fields. The department also offers a Bachelor of Arts in Cartography and GIS; students should consult with their advisor to determine which degree program is best for them.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://guide.wisc.edu/undergraduate/letters-science/geography/cartography-geographic-information-systems-bs/cartography-geographic-information-systems-bs.pdf

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Chemical Engineering
Requirements: Admission to the Bachelor of Science in Chemical Engineering is competitive and selective. The university uses a holistic review process. Applicants must meet the general UW–Madison admission requirements, which include a rigorous high school curriculum: 4 units of English, 4 units of Mathematics (including at least one unit of pre-calculus), 3–4 units of Science (including units of chemistry and physics, which are strongly recommended for engineering applicants), 3 units of Social Studies, and 2 units of a single Foreign Language. The review process also considers academic trends, extracurricular involvement, and two required essays.
Description: Chemical engineering is the study and practice of transforming matter and energy into forms that are useful to society. Chemical engineers have always been involved in the production of chemicals, but they also have roles in many other sectors, including environmental protection, energy production, pharmaceuticals and medicine, sustainable materials, and food and beverage production. For example, chemical engineers are involved in developing renewable energy sources, designing new materials for electronics and biotechnology, and creating processes for making medicines and medical devices. The program at UW–Madison is known for its strong emphasis on both fundamental principles and practical applications. Students gain a deep understanding of thermodynamics, kinetics, and transport phenomena, as well as hands-on experience in laboratory courses and design projects.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).
Accredidation: The Bachelor of Science in Chemical Engineering program at the University of Wisconsin–Madison is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org, under the commission’s General Criteria and the Program Criteria for Chemical, Biochemical, Biomolecular and Similarly Named Engineering Programs.

Requirements: To declare the major, students must have completed: CHEM 103 & CHEM 104 General Chemistry I and General Chemistry II or CHEM 109 Advanced General Chemistry or CHEM 115 & CHEM 116 Chemical Principles I and Chemical Principles II. MATH 221 Calculus and Analytic Geometry 1 or MATH 275 Topics in Calculus I. Students should contact the undergraduate chemistry advisor for further information about declaring the major.
Description: Chemistry is the science of the world at the molecular level. Its study is a quest for an understanding of the substances that comprise our world and the changes that these substances undergo. In every aspect of our lives, from the food we eat to the medicines we take, from the fuels we burn to the materials we use to build our structures, chemistry plays a central role. In the twenty-first century, the study of chemistry is more important than ever. It is the key to understanding and solving many of the challenges we face, from climate change to the development of new energy sources and the cure of diseases. The Chemistry Department at UW–Madison is a world-class institution, with a long history of excellence in research and education. Our faculty are world-renowned for their research, and they are dedicated to teaching and mentoring our students. We offer a wide range of courses and research opportunities, and our students have gone on to successful careers in a variety of fields, including medicine, law, business, and academia. Our major is designed to provide students with a strong foundation in the principles of chemistry, while also allowing them to pursue their interests in specific areas of the field. We offer a variety of courses, from introductory chemistry to advanced courses in organic, inorganic, physical, and analytical chemistry. We also offer research opportunities, which allow students to work with our faculty on cutting-edge research projects. If you are interested in chemistry, we encourage you to explore our website and learn more about our department and our major. We are confident that you will find UW–Madison to be a great place to study chemistry.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://guide.wisc.edu/undergraduate/letters-science/chemistry/chemistry-ba/
Accredidation: Students may also choose to have their degree certified by the American Chemical Society (ACS). The ACS-certified degree requires additional advanced chemistry courses beyond the minimum required for the chemistry major.

Requirements: Application for the Bachelor of Science in Chemistry is handled through the general University of Wisconsin–Madison undergraduate admission process. Requirements include a completed application (Common App or UW System Application), two required essays, official high school transcripts, and one letter of recommendation (from a teacher or counselor). Admission is based on a holistic review of academic records, including the completion of core high school subjects (English, Math, Social Science, Science, and World Language), and non-academic factors such as leadership and extracurricular involvement.
Description: Chemistry is the science of the properties, composition, and structure of substances (defined as elements and compounds), the transformations they undergo, and the energy that is released or absorbed during these processes. Chemistry is concerned with atoms as the building blocks of all matter and with the interactions of these atoms to form molecules and more complex structures. Chemistry is also sometimes referred to as “the central science” because it provides a foundation for understanding both basic and applied scientific disciplines at a fundamental level. A bachelor’s degree in chemistry opens doors to many career pathways. The chemistry major provides a gateway to a wide variety of career opportunities in many fields including, but not limited to, chemistry, medicine, law, business, and education.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).
Accredidation: Students who complete the required curriculum for the BS-Chemistry degree are certified by the American Chemical Society (ACS).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Chicanx and Latinx Studies
Requirements: To declare the major in Chicana/o and Latina/o Studies, students should meet with the department undergraduate advisor.
Description: The Chicana/o and Latina/o Studies Program (CLS) offers a systematic and interdisciplinary analysis of the Mexican- and Latin American-origin populations of the United States. Combining the methodologies of several traditional disciplines—such as history, sociology, literature, and political science—with a focus on Chicana/o and Latina/o populations, the CLS major allows students to understand how people of diverse backgrounds have shaped the history and culture of the United States. For Chicana/o and Latina/o students, the program provides a deeper understanding of their own heritage. For others, it provides an introduction to the different cultures of the U.S. and an opportunity to study the important roles that Chicanas/os and Latinas/os have played in the development of this country. CLS majors find employment in many fields—including education, law, social services, business, journalism, and government—or pursue graduate studies in a variety of disciplines.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://guide.wisc.edu/undergraduate/letters-science/chicana-chicano-latina-latino-studies/chicana-chicano-latina-latino-studies.pdf

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Chicanx and Latinx Studies
Requirements: There are no admission requirements for the major. Students may declare the major at any time. To declare, students should meet with the Chicanx and Latinx Studies advisor.
Description: The Chicanx and Latinx Studies (CLS) program offers a multidisciplinary curriculum that focuses on the Chicanx and Latinx experience in the United States. Its primary goal is to provide students with a broad-based understanding of the history, culture, and social experiences of Chicanx and Latinx people. The program also seeks to foster a critical understanding of the relationship between Chicanx and Latinx communities and the larger U.S. society, as well as the connections between Chicanx and Latinx people and other groups in the Americas. The CLS program offers an undergraduate major and certificate. The program is designed to provide students with the skills and knowledge necessary to pursue careers in a wide range of fields, including education, social work, law, medicine, business, and the arts. It also prepares students for graduate study in a variety of disciplines, including history, sociology, political science, literature, and ethnic studies.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

Requirements: To declare the Chinese major, students must first complete ASIALANG 102 First Semester Chinese or ASIALANG 110 Elementary Chinese I. Students should meet with the undergraduate advisor to discuss their interest in the major and declare the major. General university admission requires the submission of official transcripts, two essays, and an application fee. ACT or SAT scores and one letter of recommendation are optional.
Description: The Department of Asian Languages and Cultures offers a wide range of opportunities for the study of the languages and cultures of East, South, and Southeast Asia at both the undergraduate and graduate levels. Departmental course offerings include the study of languages, linguistics, literature, history, religion, folklore, and culture. The Chinese major provides students with a solid foundation in the Chinese language and its literature, culture, and history. Students can choose from a variety of courses on topics ranging from traditional poetry and fiction to contemporary cinema and popular culture. The major is designed to help students develop a high level of proficiency in Mandarin Chinese, as well as a broad understanding of the cultural and historical contexts in which the language is spoken.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

Requirements: To apply for the Bachelor of Science in Chinese, students must first be admitted to the University of Wisconsin–Madison. According to the Guide, there are no prerequisites for declaring the Chinese major, and students may declare the major at any time by contacting the undergraduate advisor. General freshman admission requirements to the university include high school transcripts, two essays, and one letter of recommendation. The university is currently test-optional through the Spring 2027 term.
Description: The Chinese major provides a program of study in Chinese language, linguistics, and literature, and in the culture and civilization of China. In addition to gaining proficiency in the language, students develop a solid understanding of the history and development of Chinese literature, as well as an appreciation of the aesthetic and cultural values that characterize the Chinese tradition. The Chinese major is also designed to provide students with the opportunity to explore other fields of study by offering a flexible curriculum.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Civil Engineering
Requirements: Students are admitted to the college through the UW–Madison Office of Admissions and Recruitment. First-year students who apply for admission to UW–Madison as a first-year student can apply for direct admission to the College of Engineering by listing a major in the College of Engineering as their first choice on the application. Students will be admitted directly to the engineering major of their choice (or as 'undeclared' in the College of Engineering) based on their application for admission to the University. Transfer students who are applying for admission to UW–Madison may also apply for direct admission to a major in the College of Engineering. Students may also be admitted to the college after they have started their studies at UW–Madison.
Description:
Civil engineering is the oldest of the engineering professions. It is the profession that provides for the basic needs of modern society: clean water, clean air, safe and efficient transportation of people and goods, and safe and reliable structures for living and working. In addition to these traditional areas, civil engineers are involved in every aspect of the protection and repair of our natural environment.

Civil engineering is a people-oriented profession. Civil engineers solve problems and design systems that directly affect the quality of life. At the University of Wisconsin–Madison, the bachelor of science degree program in civil engineering is designed to provide students with a broad foundation in the physical and engineering sciences and the flexibility to explore many of the sub-disciplines of civil engineering. Students choose electives to build a program that meets their interests in one or more of the following areas: Construction engineering and management, Environmental engineering, Geo-structural engineering, Structural engineering, Transportation engineering, Water resources engineering.

Program Educational Objectives:
1. Practice civil engineering in the private or public sector, or a related field, and contribute to the planning, design, construction, operation, or maintenance of the built environment and the protection of the natural environment.
2. Serve society by considering the environmental, social, economic, ethical, and other impacts of their work.
3. Pursue advanced education or other professional development activities and, as their careers progress, assume leadership roles.

Student Outcomes:
1. An ability to identify, formulate, and solve complex engineering problems by applying principles of engineering, science, and mathematics.
2. An ability to apply engineering design to produce solutions that meet specified needs with consideration of public health, safety, and welfare, as well as global, cultural, social, environmental, and economic factors.
3. An ability to communicate effectively with a range of audiences.
4. An ability to recognize ethical and professional responsibilities in engineering situations and make informed judgments, which must consider the impact of engineering solutions in global, economic, environmental, and societal contexts.
5. An ability to function effectively on a team whose members together provide leadership, create a collaborative and inclusive environment, establish goals, plan tasks, and meet objectives.
6. An ability to develop and conduct appropriate experimentation, analyze and interpret data, and use engineering judgment to draw conclusions.
7. An ability to acquire and apply new knowledge as needed, using appropriate learning strategies.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://guide.wisc.edu/undergraduate/engineering/civil-environmental-engineering/civil-engineering-bs/
Accredidation: Accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org, under the General Criteria and the Civil and Similarly Named Engineering Programs Program Criteria.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Classical Studies
Requirements: Admission to the Bachelor of Arts in Classical Studies program is through the general University of Wisconsin–Madison undergraduate admission process. Applicants must submit the Common Application or the UW System Application, which includes high school transcripts, two required essays, and one letter of recommendation. The university uses a holistic review process considering academic performance, course rigor, and personal factors. There are no additional entrance requirements to declare the major beyond admission to the university.
Concentration: Classical Humanities, Greek, Latin, Combined Greek and Latin
Description: Classical studies is the study of the ancient Greek and Roman worlds. At UW–Madison, this includes everything from the study of the languages (Ancient Greek, Latin, and Biblical Hebrew) to the history, literature, art, and culture of the Mediterranean world. Our department also offers courses in the civilizations of the ancient Near East and Egypt. The Classical Studies major allows students to focus their work in one of four ways: through the study of the languages (Greek, Latin, or both) or through the study of the culture (Classical Humanities). Students who major in Classical Studies will find themselves well prepared for any number of career paths. Recent graduates have gone on to careers in law, medicine, business, museum work, and education, among many others.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Classical Studies
Requirements: Admission to the Bachelor of Science in Classical Studies involves the general undergraduate application to the University of Wisconsin–Madison. The holistic review process includes academic performance (high school transcripts), two required essays, one letter of recommendation from an academic source, and extracurricular activities. ACT and SAT scores are optional through the 2026–2027 application cycles. International applicants must also demonstrate English proficiency through TOEFL, IELTS, or Duolingo English Test scores if they do not meet waiver criteria.
Concentration: Classical Humanities or The Ancient World
Description: The Classical Humanities major is designed for students who wish to explore the culture of ancient Greece and Rome and its ongoing influence on the modern world. Classical Humanities explores all aspects of ancient Greek and Roman culture, including its literature, history, art and archaeology, philosophy, and political systems. Students in the Classical Humanities major take courses in classical literature, mythology, history, art and archaeology, and philosophy; although they are not required to study ancient Greek or Latin, they may choose to do so to fulfill requirements for the major. Many students choose to double major in Classical Humanities and another subject, such as History, Art History, Political Science, Philosophy, English, or any of the sciences. A major in Classical Humanities also provides excellent preparation for students who wish to pursue a professional degree in law or medicine.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Communication Arts
Requirements: Students may declare the major at any time.
Concentration: Communication Science and Rhetorical Studies; Radio–Television–Film
Description: Communication arts explores the processes of human communication. The department’s programs are designed to provide students with a solid grounding in the theory, history, and criticism of communication, as well as the skills needed to produce and analyze messages in various media. The undergraduate major in communication arts offers two areas of study: Communication Science and Rhetorical Studies; and Radio–Television–Film.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://guide.wisc.edu/undergraduate/letters-science/communication-arts/communication-arts-ba/communication-arts-ba.pdf

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Communication Arts
Requirements: Students may declare the Communication Arts major at any time. There are no prerequisite courses or grade point average required to declare the major. To declare the major, students should meet with an advisor. To be admitted to the University of Wisconsin-Madison, applicants must submit an application through the Office of Admissions and Recruitment, which evaluates students based on academic rigor, grades, essays, and optional test scores.
Concentration: Communication Science and Rhetorical Studies; Radio-Television-Film
Description: The Department of Communication Arts is an internationally recognized center for the study and practice of human communication. In keeping with the Wisconsin Idea, the department's faculty, staff, and students strive to investigate and apply the concepts and theories of communication to the challenges of contemporary society. The department’s curriculum focuses on two main areas: Communication Science and Rhetorical Studies, and Radio-Television-Film. Within these areas, the department is committed to exploring communication as it occurs in diverse settings: in interpersonal and small group interactions; in the development and use of information technologies; in the formation and use of public discourse; and in the creation and distribution of media content. Our students develop a variety of skills, from learning how to effectively speak and write to analyzing and producing media for digital and global audiences.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Communication Sciences and Disorders
Requirements: To declare the major in communication sciences and disorders, students must have a cumulative GPA of 3.000 or better. Students who do not have a 3.000 GPA may still declare if they have completed CS&D 201, CS&D 202, and CS&D 240 with a GPA of 3.000 or better in these three courses. Students must complete a declaration of major form found on the Department of Communication Sciences and Disorders website.
Description: Communication sciences and disorders is the study of the processes and disorders of human communication. The undergraduate program in communication sciences and disorders (CS&D) is designed to provide students with a broad-based education in the physical, biological, and social science bases of human communication. Students will learn about the development and use of speech, language, and hearing, as well as the nature and management of communication disorders across the lifespan. The program provides a solid foundation for students planning to pursue graduate study in speech-language pathology or audiology, which is required for professional practice in the field. The major also provides a strong background for students interested in careers in related fields such as education, health care, and social services.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://guide.wisc.edu/undergraduate/letters-science/communication-sciences-disorders/communication-sciences-disorders_degreesmajorscertificatestext.pdf

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Communication Sciences and Disorders
Requirements: To declare the major, students must have completed CS&D 201 and CS&D 202 with a grade of C or better (or B or better if taken at another institution) and have a cumulative GPA of 3.000 or better. Students must be in good academic standing (2.000 GPA or better) in order to declare. The Bachelor of Science in Communication Sciences and Disorders requires a total of 120 credits, including University General Education Requirements and College of Letters & Science Degree Requirements. The major specifically requires 30 credits, including core courses CS&D 201, CS&D 202, CS&D 210, CS&D 240, CS&D 315, CS&D 318, CS&D 371, and CS&D 440, plus at least 6 elective credits. Students must maintain a 2.000 GPA in all CS&D courses and 15 upper-level major credits must be completed in residence.
Description: The Department of Communication Sciences and Disorders (CS&D) offers two undergraduate majors: one in the College of Letters & Science (L&S) and one in the School of Education (SoE). Both programs provide students with a strong foundation in the basic sciences of human communication (speech, language, and hearing) and an introduction to the disorders of communication. The curriculum includes coursework in the biological, physical, social, and psychological bases of communication and how these are affected by disorders across the lifespan. The undergraduate major in CS&D provides an excellent background for students who wish to pursue graduate study in speech-language pathology or audiology. It also provides a strong foundation for students who wish to pursue careers in other fields, such as education, health care, or research.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://guide.wisc.edu/undergraduate/letters-science/communication-sciences-disorders/communication-sciences-disorders-bs/communication-sciences-disorders-bs_requirementstext.pdf

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Community and Environmental Sociology
Requirements: To apply for the Bachelor of Science in Community and Environmental Sociology, students must apply for undergraduate admission to the University of Wisconsin–Madison. Applicants must submit the Common Application or the Universities of Wisconsin Application, which includes two required essays, official high school transcripts, and an optional letter of recommendation. Required high school coursework includes 4 units of English, 4 units of Mathematics, 3 units of Social Science, 3 units of Science, and 2 units of a single Foreign Language. Once admitted to the university, students in the College of Agricultural and Life Sciences (CALS) can declare the major by meeting with the department's undergraduate advisor.
Department: College of Agricultural and Life Sciences
Description: How do communities deal with rapid change? How can we balance the needs of the environment with the needs of the economy? How do our neighborhoods and food systems affect our health? These are the types of questions community and environmental sociologists ask. The major in community and environmental sociology provides students with the conceptual and methodological tools to understand the social dimensions of environmental and resource issues and the processes of community and social change. Students choose from courses on a variety of topics, including the environment, food and agriculture, community development, health, and social inequality. Community and environmental sociology is a versatile major that prepares students for careers in government, non-profits, or the private sector, as well as for graduate or professional school in such areas as law, urban and regional planning, public health, and sociology.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Community and Nonprofit Leadership
Requirements: All undergraduate students apply through the Office of Admissions and Recruitment. Freshmen and transfer students may be admitted directly to the Community and Nonprofit Leadership major by indicating it as their first choice on their application. Requirements for a complete application include the Common Application or UW System Application, two required essays, official high school transcripts, and one letter of recommendation. The university is currently test-optional.
Description: The Community and Nonprofit Leadership (CNL) major is for students who want to be leaders and changemakers in their communities. Grounded in the School of Human Ecology’s commitment to improving the quality of life for individuals, families, and communities, the CNL major prepares students for leadership roles in nonprofit organizations and community-based agencies. CNL students gain an understanding of the nonprofit sector and the role it plays in addressing social issues and creating positive change. The curriculum emphasizes social justice, community engagement, and leadership development. Students learn how to analyze social problems, develop strategies for change, and lead and manage nonprofit organizations. The CNL major also emphasizes practical, hands-on experience through a required internship.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Computer Engineering
Requirements: To apply for the Bachelor of Science in Computer Engineering, applicants must submit the Common Application or the Universities of Wisconsin Application.
