Required materials include official high school transcripts, two essays (a personal statement and a statement of interest in UW-Madison), and one letter of recommendation from an academic source. The University of Wisconsin–Madison is test-optional for ACT and SAT scores through the Summer 2027 term. Engineering applicants are expected to have strong preparation in mathematics and science, including courses in physics and chemistry.
Description: Computer engineering is a field of study that encompasses the design and development of computer systems and their components. This includes hardware components, such as processors and memory systems, as well as software components, such as operating systems and compilers. Computer engineers apply the principles of computer science and electrical engineering to the design, development, and maintenance of computer systems. They are involved in everything from the design of individual microprocessors to the development of complex computer networks. The curriculum for a computer engineering degree typically includes courses in computer architecture, digital logic design, computer networks, operating systems, and software engineering. Graduates with a degree in computer engineering can work in a variety of industries, including telecommunications, aerospace, and consumer electronics. They may also pursue advanced degrees in computer engineering or related fields. The bachelor of science in computer engineering degree program is designed to provide students with a strong foundation in both the hardware and software aspects of computer systems. Students learn about digital logic design, computer architecture, operating systems, programming languages, and software engineering. They also gain experience with a variety of computer systems, from small embedded systems to large-scale data centers.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).
Accredidation: The Bachelor of Science in Computer Engineering at the University of Wisconsin–Madison is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org, under the commission’s General Criteria and Program Criteria for Computer and Similarly Named Engineering Programs.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Computer Sciences
Requirements: To declare the Computer Sciences major, students must have completed COMP SCI 300 and either MATH 222 or MATH 276 with a grade of C or better. General admission to the University of Wisconsin-Madison is also required, which involves a holistic review of academic records, two required essays, and a list of extracurricular activities. The university is test-optional for the ACT and SAT through the Spring 2027 term.
Description: The Department of Computer Sciences is among the oldest and top-ranked computer science departments in the world. It offers a Bachelor of Science and a Bachelor of Arts in Computer Sciences. The department’s faculty are leaders in their fields, and its graduates are in high demand across a variety of industries. Computer science is one of the most popular majors on campus, and the number of students majoring in the subject has grown exponentially in recent years. Computer science is the study of computers and computing, including their theoretical and algorithmic foundations, hardware and software, and their uses for processing information. The discipline of computer science includes the study of algorithms and data structures, computer and network design, modeling data and information processes, and artificial intelligence. Computer science draws some of its foundations from mathematics and engineering and therefore incorporates techniques from areas such as probability, statistics, and electronic circuit design.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Computer Sciences
Requirements: To apply for undergraduate admission to the Bachelor of Science in Computer Sciences, applicants must submit the Common Application or the UW System Application, which includes two required essays, high school transcripts, and an application fee. One letter of recommendation is optional but encouraged. While not required for admission to the university, declaring the Computer Sciences major requires completion of specific prerequisite courses (including COMP SCI 300 and MATH 221) with a grade of C or better.
Description: Computer sciences is the study of computers and computing, including their theoretical and algorithmic foundations, hardware and software, and their applications for processing information. The discipline of computer science includes the study of algorithms and data structures, computer and network design, modeling data and information processes, and artificial intelligence. Computer science draws some of its foundations from mathematics and engineering and therefore incorporates techniques from areas such as queueing theory, probability and statistics, and electronic circuit design. Computer science also makes heavy use of hypothesis testing and experimentation during the conceptualization, design, measurement, and refinement of new algorithms, information structures, and computer architectures.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Conservation Biology
Requirements: Applicants must first be admitted to the University of Wisconsin-Madison. For undergraduate admission, the university requires the completion of the Common Application or the UW System Application, high school and/or college transcripts, two essays, and one letter of recommendation. There are no specific requirements to declare the Conservation Biology major; students may declare at any time by meeting with an advisor. The program is available as either a Bachelor of Arts or a Bachelor of Science.
Description: The Conservation Biology major was established in 1988 to provide a formal program of study for students interested in the biological aspects of conserving the earth's biodiversity. The program is an interdisciplinary collaboration between several departments (primarily Botany and Integrative Biology), and includes a wide range of courses from these and other departments (e.g., Forest and Wildlife Ecology, Entomology, Geography, Genetics, and others). The curriculum is designed to provide students with a broad background in the biological sciences, with an emphasis on ecology, genetics, and evolution. Students also take courses in the social sciences and humanities to gain an understanding of the human dimensions of conservation. The program is intended to prepare students for graduate study in conservation biology or related fields, or for careers in conservation-related agencies and organizations.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Conservation Biology
Requirements: To apply for the Bachelor of Science in Conservation Biology at the University of Wisconsin–Madison, applicants must submit a completed application which includes two application essays (a personal statement and an essay about interest in the university), official high school transcripts, and at least one letter of recommendation. Standardized test scores (ACT or SAT) are optional for students applying through the Spring 2025 term.
Description: The conservation biology major is designed to provide students with a broad-based foundation in the biological, environmental, and social sciences as they apply to the conservation of biodiversity. Students are encouraged to use this major as a gateway to professional careers in conservation and environmental management, or as a preparation for graduate study in a range of fields including ecology, evolutionary biology, environmental science, and policy. The major is interdisciplinary and draws from courses across several departments in the College of Letters & Science and the College of Agricultural and Life Sciences. The requirements include foundation courses in biology, chemistry, and mathematics, and a series of core and elective courses in ecology, genetics, and the social sciences.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://www.uwgb.edu/

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Consumer Finance and Financial Planning
Requirements: All students who apply to the University of Wisconsin–Madison and indicate an interest in a major offered by the School of Human Ecology will be considered for admission to the school. For more information, please see the Office of Admissions and Recruitment website. Students who are already on campus and would like to declare a major in the School of Human Ecology should visit the SoHE website for information on the declaration process.
Description: The major in Consumer Finance and Financial Planning prepares students for careers as financial planners or in other areas of financial services. Students in this major study the financial issues that individuals and families encounter and learn to help them achieve their financial goals through the study of insurance, investments, taxes, retirement, and estate planning. The Consumer Finance and Financial Planning major is a CFP Board-Registered Program. This means that students who complete the major meet the education requirement to sit for the CFP® Certification Examination.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://guide.wisc.edu/undergraduate/undergraduate.pdf
Accredidation: CFP Board-Registered Program

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Consumer Marketplace Studies
Requirements: Admissions to the Consumer Marketplace Studies major is a two-step process. First, students must be admitted to the University of Wisconsin–Madison. Second, students must be admitted to the School of Human Ecology. All students who apply to the University of Wisconsin–Madison as either a first-year or student and who list Consumer Marketplace Studies as their first choice of major will be admitted directly to the major in the School of Human Ecology. Currently enrolled UW–Madison students can also apply for admission to the major. Students must have a 2.75 cumulative GPA.
Description: The Consumer Behavior and Marketplace Studies major prepares students for professional careers in the diverse and ever-evolving world of retail and related industries. This major focuses on the role of the consumer in the marketplace and how the marketplace functions. Coursework includes classes in retailing, marketing, business, and consumer behavior, as well as analytics, communication, and social science. Students in the program have opportunities to gain professional experience through internships and study abroad. Graduates of the program are well-prepared for roles such as buyer, planner, marketing analyst, retail manager, and more.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://guide.wisc.edu/undergraduate/human-ecology/consumer-science/consumer-behavior-marketplace-studies-bs/

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Dairy Science
Requirements: Admission to the Bachelor of Science in Dairy Science program follows the general University of Wisconsin–Madison undergraduate admission requirements. These include the submission of a completed application, two required essays, official high school transcripts, and an application fee or waiver. Recommended high school coursework includes 4 units of English, 4 units of Mathematics, 3 units of Social Science, 3 units of Science, and 2 units of a single Foreign Language. One letter of recommendation and ACT/SAT scores are optional.
Department: College of Agricultural and Life Sciences
Description: Dairy science is the study of the milk-producing animals—their care, management, and the business of dairy production. The major in Dairy Science provides students with a solid foundation in the biological sciences and their application to the dairy industry. Students learn about genetics, nutrition, physiology, and the business of dairy farming. The Dairy Science major is flexible, allowing students to tailor their studies to their interests and career goals. Whether students are interested in veterinary medicine, research, dairy production, or agribusiness, the Dairy Science major provides the knowledge and skills necessary for success. The Dairy Science major also provides students with many opportunities for hands-on learning outside the classroom. Students can participate in internships, research projects, and student organizations like the Badger Dairy Club. These experiences allow students to gain practical experience and network with professionals in the dairy industry.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://catalog.calpoly.edu/agriculture-food-environmental-sciences/animal-science/dairy-science-bs/

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Data Science
Requirements: To apply for the Bachelor of Arts in Data Science, students must first be admitted to the University of Wisconsin-Madison. For admission to the university, applicants must submit a completed application, official transcripts, and two required essays. To declare the major in Data Science, students must have a cumulative GPA of at least 2.0 and have completed the following courses with a grade of C or better: Calculus (MATH 221 or equivalent), Programming (COMP SCI 220 or equivalent), and Statistics (STAT 240 or equivalent).
Description: The Data Science major was created in response to the massive data being generated in almost every sector of our society—from commerce and business to precision medicine and social media. The program is a collaboration between the Department of Statistics and the Department of Computer Sciences. Students in the Data Science major will learn how to: integrate, manage, and mine data; use statistical and machine learning methods to analyze data; and communicate their findings effectively. The program is designed to be flexible, allowing students to combine their interest in data science with other fields of study.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Data Science
Requirements: To declare the Data Science major, students must have completed the following courses with a grade of C or better: COMP SCI 220 Data Science Programming I or COMP SCI 300 Programming II and III; and one of the following MATH courses: MATH 222 Calculus and Analytic Geometry 2 or MATH 276 Calculus and Analytic Geometry 2. Students may declare the major at any time after these requirements are met.
Description: The Data Science major at UW–Madison has been developed through a collaboration between the Department of Statistics and the Department of Computer Sciences. In today’s world, data is being generated at an unprecedented rate, and organizations are increasingly relying on data-driven insights to make informed decisions. Data science is the field that combines statistics, computer science, and domain expertise to extract knowledge and insights from data. The Data Science major provides students with a strong foundation in these areas, as well as the skills needed to work with large and complex datasets. Students will learn how to collect, manage, and analyze data, as well as how to communicate their findings to a variety of audiences. The major is designed to be flexible, allowing students to pursue their interests in a variety of application areas.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

Requirements: There are no additional admission requirements for the Economics major. Students may declare the major at any time as long as they are currently enrolled at UW-Madison. Students are encouraged to declare early so they may benefit from the major's advising services. To declare the major, students should meet with an advisor.
Description: Economics is the study of how people, firms, and governments make choices and how those choices determine how resources are used. Economics is a social science that uses a variety of methods—including mathematical and statistical techniques—to analyze topics ranging from individual decision making to the behavior of entire economies. Economics provides students with a strong foundation in analytical and critical thinking, which is valuable in a wide range of careers in business, government, and law. Undergraduates in economics can choose between two majors: Economics, B.A. and Economics, B.S. In either major, students may choose the regular economics major or the option in Mathematical Economic Analysis. The regular major is a great choice for students who want to develop a strong understanding of economic principles and their applications to the real world. The Mathematical Economic Analysis option is designed for students who want to develop a more rigorous mathematical and statistical background in economics. This option is excellent preparation for graduate study in economics or a related field.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://guide.wisc.edu/undergraduate/letters-science/economics/

Requirements: Students may declare the Economics major if they have: At least a 2.000 GPA in economics courses taken at UW-Madison; At least a 2.000 cumulative GPA at UW-Madison.
Description: Economics is the study of how people, organizations, and societies use their scarce resources. It is a social science that uses the tools of mathematics and statistics to study how people behave and how the world works. Economics is also about analyzing how policy, incentives, and different institutional structures affect people’s lives. Students in the economics major at UW–Madison develop skills in critical thinking, data analysis, and problem-solving, which they can use to understand and address a wide range of social and economic issues. Economics is a versatile major that prepares students for a wide range of careers in business, government, and the non-profit sector, as well as for graduate study in economics, law, and other fields.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://guide.wisc.edu/undergraduate/letters-science/economics/economics-bs/

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Education Studies
Requirements: The Education Studies program does not have a formal application for students currently enrolled at UW–Madison. Students can declare the Education Studies major after meeting with a School of Education advisor. Prospective students not yet enrolled at UW–Madison must first be admitted to the university; for information on the university's application process, visit the Office of Admissions and Recruitment website.
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Education Studies is designed for students who are interested in the study of education and its role in society. The major provides a strong foundation in the social and historical aspects of education, with an emphasis on how education and schooling have shaped and continue to shape our society. Students will learn to analyze educational issues from multiple perspectives and to understand the role of education in promoting social justice and equality. The Education Studies major is not a teacher certification program; however, it provides a strong foundation for students who may later pursue a teaching certificate or graduate studies in education or related fields.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Electrical Engineering
Requirements: Admission to the College of Engineering is a two-step process. First, applicants must be admitted to the University of Wisconsin–Madison. Second, students must be admitted to the College of Engineering. Students who choose a major in the College of Engineering when they apply to the University of Wisconsin–Madison will be considered for direct admission to that major. Direct admission is competitive and selective. Decisions are based on a holistic review of each application. Factors considered include academic preparation (including the rigor of the high school curriculum), grade point average, class rank, and ACT or SAT scores (if provided), and other information available in the application (including the required essays).
Description: Electrical engineering (EE) is the study of the design and manufacture of computer systems, microelectronics, power and energy, communications, and signal processing. The semiconductor industry is a key component of our modern life, which provides the technology and infrastructure for most electronic devices and applications. With the global shortage of semiconductor chips and the national effort to boost domestic production, there is a high demand for skilled engineers who can design, fabricate, and test semiconductor devices and circuits. The Semiconductor Engineering named option is a specialized track within the B.S. Electrical Engineering program that prepares students for careers in this rapidly growing and vital sector. The curriculum covers the fundamental principles and the state-of-the-art techniques of semiconductor materials, physics, devices, fabrication, and circuit design. Students will also gain hands-on experience through laboratory courses and projects that involve cutting-edge facilities and tools. By completing this program, students will acquire the knowledge and skills necessary to contribute to the innovation and excellence of the semiconductor industry.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://guide.wisc.edu/undergraduate/engineering/electrical-computer-engineering/electrical-engineering-bs/electrical-engineering-semiconductor-engineering-bs/
Accredidation: The Bachelor of Science in Electrical Engineering program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org, under the General Criteria and the Program Criteria for Electrical, Computer, Communications, Telecommunication(s) and Similarly Named Engineering Programs.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Education in Elementary Education
Requirements: Prospective students apply for the program by indicating their interest in Elementary Education: Kindergarten–9th Grade on the university application. In the event that the number of applicants exceeds program capacity, a competitive selection process will be implemented. Application requirements for on-campus students include: Current UW–Madison student; GPA of at least 2.5 based on UW–Madison coursework; Completed online application. The application will ask students to provide a list of experiences and a personal statement.
Description: Students in the Elementary Education: Kindergarten–9th Grade (K–9) program learn to teach all subjects in grades K–9. This program prepares students to meet the requirements for licensure to teach in Wisconsin public schools. The curriculum provides a strong foundation in the core subjects—language arts, mathematics, science, and social studies—and explores the most effective ways to teach them. In addition to a focus on academic subjects, students in the Elementary Education program study child development, educational psychology, and social justice. Starting early in the program, students participate in field experiences in local classrooms, working with students and teachers. The program culminates in a full-semester student teaching experience where students apply the knowledge and skills they have gained to teach in their own classroom.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://guide.wisc.edu/undergraduate/education/curriculum-instruction/elementary-education-bse/elementary-education-kindergarten-9th-grade-bse/

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Engineering Mechanics
Requirements: To apply for admission to the Bachelor of Science in Engineering Mechanics, students must apply through the UW-Madison Office of Admissions and Recruitment. Applicants should list Engineering Mechanics as their first choice of major on the application. Admission is based on a holistic review that considers the rigor of the high school curriculum (with a particular focus on math and science), academic performance, and personal essays. Requirements include the completion of the Common Application, two mandatory essays, and the submission of official high school transcripts. ACT or SAT scores and letters of recommendation are optional components of the application.
Description: Engineering mechanics is the study of forces and the resulting deformations, accelerations, motions, vibrations and other responses they cause. It is the backbone of many engineering disciplines. It is vital to the design and analysis of any system where energy, forces and motions are important. Examples include the design of aircraft and spacecraft, micro-electromechanical systems (MEMS), car engines, human prosthetics and bridge structures. Engineering mechanics provides a rigorous and solid foundation for many engineering careers and is the basis for most of the mechanical engineering program. The bachelor of science in engineering mechanics degree is for students who have an interest in mathematics and the physical sciences and wish to explore the application of these subjects to the design and analysis of complex engineering systems. The curriculum provides a strong foundation in mathematics and physics and their application in the various areas of mechanics: statics, dynamics, mechanics of materials, fluid mechanics and vibrations. Students learn to use mathematical and computational tools to solve problems and to design and conduct experiments. The curriculum also provides students with the opportunity to explore other areas of engineering through technical electives. The program is designed to prepare students for careers in a wide range of industries, including aerospace, automotive, energy and manufacturing, as well as for graduate study in engineering and related fields.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).
Accredidation: The Bachelor of Science in Engineering Mechanics program is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org, under the commission’s General Criteria and Program Criteria for Engineering Mechanics and Similarly Named Engineering Programs.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Engineering Physics
Requirements: Undergraduate admission to the Bachelor of Science in Engineering Physics is managed through the Office of Admissions and Recruitment. The application process involves a holistic review that considers academic excellence (rigor of curriculum and grades), two required essays, and extracurricular activities. Applicants may submit the Common Application or the UW System Application. One letter of recommendation is optional, and ACT or SAT scores are also optional for students applying through the Spring 2025 term.
Concentration: Plasma Science and Engineering, Scientific Computing, and Engineering Physics Research
Description: The Engineering Physics (EP) program at the University of Wisconsin–Madison is one of only a few such programs in the United States. EP is an interdisciplinary program that combines a broad-based foundation in physics and mathematics with a strong emphasis on engineering applications. The EP program is designed to prepare students for careers in high-technology industries, research and development, and for graduate study in engineering or physics. The curriculum is flexible and allows students to tailor their studies to their interests. Students in the EP program can choose from three focus areas: Plasma Science and Engineering, Scientific Computing, and Engineering Physics Research.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).
Accredidation: The Bachelor of Science in Engineering Physics is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org, under the commission’s general criteria.

Requirements: The English major is open to all students at UW-Madison. Students are encouraged to declare early, especially if they have an interest in one of the certificates, such as Creative Writing. To declare a major in English, please schedule an appointment with an undergraduate advisor.
Description:
English is the study of literature and language in their many forms, including poetry, prose, drama, film, and digital media. Students of English learn to read closely, to write clearly and persuasively, and to think critically and creatively. They explore the history of the language, the social and political contexts of literature, and the diversity of human experience reflected in the written word.

The Department of English at UW–Madison offers two tracks: English (with an emphasis on literature and language) and Creative Writing. Both tracks are designed to provide students with a broad and deep understanding of literature and language, and to prepare them for a wide range of careers in fields such as education, journalism, law, business, and the arts.

Beyond the classroom, our students can gain experience with literary publishing (as editors and contributors to The Madison Review), work as writing peer mentors, and participate in a range of activities sponsored by our student-led English Undergraduate Student Association (EUSA).
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://guide.wisc.edu/undergraduate/letters-science/english/

Requirements: Applicants for the Bachelor of Science in English must complete the University of Wisconsin–Madison freshman application. Required materials include the Common Application (which includes two required essays), official high school transcripts, and an application fee. One letter of recommendation is optional. There are no additional admission requirements specifically for the English major beyond the general university admission criteria; however, students must be admitted to the College of Letters & Science and then declare the major.
Description: The Department of English offers a wide-ranging program of study in literature, the English language, and creative and expository writing. Since its inception in 1860, the department has been a site of innovation in teaching and research, and it remains today one of the most distinguished departments in the country. Students in the department can choose from among two options: the major in English and the major in English with a creative writing emphasis. Within these majors, students have the opportunity to study a variety of literatures in English as well as the history and structure of the English language. They may explore the range of genres, from traditional ones such as poetry and drama to newer ones such as digital media and film. They will study canonical authors and also have the opportunity to delve into the literatures of historically marginalized groups. They will write poems and stories, analyze the structure of sentence and verse, and learn to make complex and persuasive arguments in writing.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, need-based, and departmental (English Department scholarships)

Requirements: To declare this major, students must be admitted to UW–Madison and the College of Agricultural and Life Sciences (CALS). All students who meet this criteria may declare the major.
Department: College of Agricultural and Life Sciences
Description: Entomology is the study of insects, their relationship to humans, other organisms, and the environment. Insects are the most diverse group of organisms on Earth. They are found in nearly every environment and play many vital roles in the ecosystem. Some insects are important pollinators, others are pests of crops or transmit diseases, and some are used in research to help us understand biological processes. The entomology major is designed to provide students with a broad background in the biological and environmental sciences. The program emphasizes the study of insects, but also includes coursework in other areas of biology, chemistry, physics, and mathematics. Students in the entomology major have the opportunity to participate in research, internships, and other hands-on learning experiences. Graduates of the program are prepared for careers in a variety of fields, including agriculture, public health, environmental science, and education. They are also well-prepared for graduate study in entomology or other biological sciences.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://guide.wisc.edu/undergraduate/agricultural-life-sciences/entomology/entomology-bs/entomology-bs.pdf

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Environmental Sciences
Requirements: The Environmental Sciences major is open to any undergraduate student at UW–Madison. Students may choose to earn the major in the College of Agricultural and Life Sciences (CALS) or the College of Letters & Science (L&S). In CALS, the major is a Bachelor of Science (B.S.) degree. In L&S, the major can be a Bachelor of Arts (B.A.) or a Bachelor of Science (B.S.) degree. Students are encouraged to meet with an advisor to discuss the requirements and declare the major.
Description: Environmental sciences is an interdisciplinary program that provides a broad-based, rigorous science background for students who want to understand the environment and develop solutions to environmental problems. The major is offered through both the College of Agricultural and Life Sciences (CALS) and the College of Letters & Science (L&S). The program integrates knowledge from across the biological and physical sciences, including chemistry, biology, physics, and mathematics, to study the environment and find solutions to environmental problems. The curriculum consists of a core of foundation courses, introductory and capstone courses in environmental science, and a wide range of elective courses allowing students to tailor their education to specific interests such as ecology, atmospheric sciences, geosciences, or water resources. Students will learn to integrate knowledge from various scientific disciplines to understand environmental systems, use scientific methods to design studies and analyze results, and apply scientific knowledge to address critical environmental issues.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://guide.wisc.edu/undergraduate/undergraduate.pdf

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Environmental Sciences
Requirements: Applicants must meet general University of Wisconsin–Madison undergraduate admission requirements. These include the completion of high school coursework (4 units of English, 4 units of Mathematics, 3 units of Social Studies, 3 units of Natural Science, and 2 units of a single Foreign Language). Application materials required include the high school transcript, two essays, and one letter of recommendation (optional). The Environmental Sciences program is co-sponsored by the College of Agricultural and Life Sciences and the College of Letters & Science.
Department: College of Agricultural and Life Sciences; College of Letters & Science
Description: Environmental Science is an interdisciplinary field that investigates the processes that control the environment, the impacts of human activities on these processes, and the implications of environmental change for the health and well-being of the planet. The Environmental Sciences major provides a rigorous science-based curriculum that prepares students to address some of the most pressing environmental challenges of our time. Students in the major gain a strong foundation in the physical, biological, and social sciences, and develop the skills needed to analyze and solve environmental problems. The curriculum includes core courses in biology, chemistry, physics, and mathematics, as well as specialized courses in environmental science, such as atmospheric science, ecology, geology, and soil science. Students also have the opportunity to participate in research and internships, providing hands-on experience in the field.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Environmental Studies
Requirements: The environmental studies major is a secondary major. Students must also complete a primary major in another field. Students in good standing may declare the environmental studies major at any time. To declare the major, students must meet with an academic advisor. Students in the environmental studies major earn either a bachelor of arts (B.A.) or a bachelor of science (B.S.) degree, as determined by their primary major.
Description: The Environmental Studies major is a unique, additional major that must be paired with another major. This interdisciplinary approach allows students to explore the environment through many different lenses – including history, ethics, economics, ecology, and more – and build the tools to address our world’s most pressing environmental challenges. Because students pair environmental studies with another major, they are able to integrate environmental perspectives into any field of study, from business and engineering to history and the arts. This creates a flexible and diverse learning environment that helps students see the environment from many perspectives and gives them the skills to solve problems in a variety of fields. Through this program, students learn to think across boundaries through coursework in the humanities, social sciences, and natural sciences; understand the complex relationship between humans and the environment; tackle real-world environmental problems; and gain skills in research, writing, and communication.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://nelson.wisc.edu/undergraduate/environmental-studies-major/

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Environmental Studies
Requirements: To apply for the Bachelor of Science in Environmental Studies, students must first be admitted to the University of Wisconsin–Madison. Freshmen application requirements include the Common Application or the UW System Application, two required essays, high school transcripts, and one letter of recommendation (optional). Standardized test scores (ACT/SAT) are optional through the Spring 2025 term. Once enrolled at UW-Madison, the Environmental Studies major is open to any undergraduate student. To declare the major, students must meet with an undergraduate advisor to discuss requirements and complete the declaration process.
Description: Environmental studies is a co-major. It must be taken in conjunction with another undergraduate major. Students may choose any other major offered at UW–Madison. Environmental studies provides a unique opportunity to look at any major through an environmental lens. Environmental studies is a flexible, interdisciplinary major that can be paired with any other major on campus, from biology or community and environmental sociology to history, business, or engineering. Students in environmental studies work to understand the complex interactions between humans and nature. They develop the skills and knowledge to address environmental problems from multiple perspectives—scientific, social, and humanistic. The program's interdisciplinary approach prepares students to be informed citizens and leaders in a wide range of fields. The Nelson Institute for Environmental Studies was established in 1970 and renamed in 2002 to honor former Wisconsin governor and U.S. Senator Gaylord Nelson, the founder of Earth Day. The institute serves as a campus-wide hub for interdisciplinary environmental initiatives, and it is a national leader in environmental education and research.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Business Administration in Finance, Investment and Banking
Requirements: Students can apply for the Bachelor of Business Administration (BBA) through three different paths: Direct Admit from High School, Pre-Business Admissions, and Transfer Students. For more information on the application and current requirements, please see the Wisconsin School of Business undergraduate website.
Description: The Finance major prepares students for careers in corporate financial management, commercial and investment banking, and investment management. Students develop an understanding of the concepts of valuation, risk-return trade-offs, financial statement analysis, and capital structure. They are also introduced to the analysis and evaluation of investments such as common stocks, fixed income securities, and derivatives. In addition, students study the operations and roles of financial markets and institutions in a global context. The major also provides an understanding of how businesses and individual investors obtain and manage financial resources. Finance students develop their analytical and problem-solving skills using various methodologies and tools including spreadsheets, databases, and financial modeling.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://guide.wisc.edu/undergraduate/business/finance/business-finance-investment-banking-bba/

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Food Science
Requirements: To declare the Food Science major, students must make an appointment with the food science advisor. Contact information can be found on the 'Advising and Careers' tab. Students can declare the Food Science major as a first-year student or at any time in their undergraduate career.
Department: College of Agricultural and Life Sciences
Description: Food science is a multidisciplinary field that applies chemistry, microbiology, engineering, and nutrition to develop new food products and design processes to improve the safety and quality of food. The food science major at UW–Madison is known for its rigorous curriculum, which prepares students for careers in the food industry, government, and academia. Students in the program learn about food chemistry, food microbiology, food engineering, and food processing. They also gain hands-on experience in the department's state-of-the-art pilot plants and laboratories. The program is designed to meet the standards set by the Institute of Food Technologists (IFT), ensuring that students receive a high-quality education that is recognized by employers worldwide.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://guide.wisc.edu/undergraduate/agricultural-life-sciences/food-science/food-science-bs/
Accredidation: The Food Science major is approved by the Higher Education Review Board (HERB) of the Institute of Food Technologists (IFT).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Forest Science
Requirements: Admissions to the major is handled through the Office of Admissions and Recruitment. All students are admitted as pre-majors. Once admitted to the college, students must meet with an advisor to declare the major.
Department: College of Agricultural and Life Sciences
Description: Society's need for forest products and the desire for diverse forest-based services—such as clean water, wildlife habitat, and outdoor recreation—continue to grow. To meet these demands, the forest science major is designed to provide students with the knowledge and skills they need to manage forest resources sustainably and for the benefit of all. The forest science major is a professional program that emphasizes the economic, social, and environmental aspects of forest management. Students learn to apply the principles of ecology, biology, and the physical sciences to the management of forest ecosystems. Graduates are prepared for careers in forest management, conservation, and research with government agencies, non-profit organizations, and private companies. The forest science major is accredited by the Society of American Foresters (SAF).
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://guide.wisc.edu/undergraduate/agricultural-life-sciences/forest-wildlife-ecology/forest-science-bs/
Accredidation: The forest science major is accredited by the Society of American Foresters (SAF).

Requirements: To declare the French major, students must have completed or be currently enrolled in FRENCH 204 or equivalent. Students should meet with the undergraduate advisor to discuss their interest in the major. Applicants must also meet general University of Wisconsin-Madison undergraduate admission requirements, which include high school transcripts, two essays, and an optional letter of recommendation.
Description: The French major at UW–Madison allows students to improve their French language skills while exploring the literature, culture, and history of the French-speaking world. In our courses, students develop proficiency in communication and gain an understanding of the diversity of the Francophone world. Beyond the classroom, students may choose to live in the French-speaking wing of the International Learning Community (the French House), participate in the French Club, or attend the weekly French conversation table (the Café Français). Many students also choose to study abroad in a French-speaking country, which is an excellent way to immerse themselves in the language and culture. Students who major in French are prepared for a variety of careers in fields such as international business, government, education, law, and the non-profit sector. French is an official language in 29 countries and is one of the official languages of the United Nations, the European Union, and the International Olympic Committee.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://www.admissions.txst.edu/explore/academics/majors-and-degrees.html

Requirements: Applicants must complete the Common Application or the UW System Application. Application requirements include official high school transcripts, one required essay, and an application fee. Submission of ACT or SAT scores and one letter of recommendation are optional for undergraduate admission. Students interested in the French major typically apply for general admission to the College of Letters & Science and may declare the major after meeting with a department advisor.
Description: The Department of French and Italian offers a wide range of opportunities for the study of French and Italian languages and literatures. These programs are designed to provide students with a comprehensive knowledge of the language and culture of France and Francophone countries and of Italy. French is a major language of international culture, being one of the official languages of the United Nations, and is spoken by more than 200 million people on five continents. Students will find that the study of French or Italian is a great goal in itself and a wonderful complement to many other majors in the humanities, social sciences, and sciences. For students interested in international studies, French or Italian is a natural fit. More than half of French majors at UW–Madison are double majors. The Department of French and Italian is committed to providing students with an understanding of French and Italian cultures in a global context. The department offers courses in language, literature, culture, and film, and its programs are designed to meet the needs of students with a variety of goals.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Gender and Women's Studies
Requirements: Students may declare the major at any time by meeting with an advisor in the department. Students should complete at least one GWS course before declaring the major. It is also recommended that students meet with an advisor to discuss the major requirements and their progress.
Description: Gender and women's studies is an interdisciplinary field that challenges us to consider how our lives are shaped by gender. Students analyze the impact of gender and its intersection with other social categories—such as race, class, ethnicity, sexuality, and disability—within our legal, economic, and political systems, as well as in our homes, our communities, and our own bodies. Gender and women’s studies courses cover a wide range of topics, including feminist theory, women’s history, LGBTQ+ studies, global feminism, and gender and health. The Gender and Women’s Studies major at UW–Madison is one of the oldest and most respected programs in the country. Our faculty are leading scholars in their fields, and our students are passionate about making a difference in the world. A major in gender and women’s studies provides students with strong critical thinking, writing, and research skills that are highly valued by employers in a variety of fields, including law, medicine, social work, education, and public policy. Our graduates go on to successful careers in a wide range of areas, including non-profit organizations, government agencies, and the private sector.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://guide.wisc.edu/undergraduate/letters-science/gender-womens-studies/gender-womens-studies-ba/
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, Need-based, Research-based, and Travel awards

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Gender and Women's Studies
Requirements: To apply for undergraduate admission to the University of Wisconsin–Madison, applicants must submit the following: the Common Application or the UW System Application, two required essays, official high school transcripts, and at least one letter of recommendation (up to two are accepted). Students may also submit ACT or SAT scores, though they are currently optional for applicants through the Spring 2027 term. Students in the College of Letters & Science can declare the Gender and Women’s Studies major by meeting with the department undergraduate advisor.
Description: The Department of Gender and Women's Studies is a vibrant community of students and scholars at the University of Wisconsin–Madison. Since its creation in 1975, the department has grown into a world-renowned program that offers students many opportunities to explore how we live our lives as gendered beings in a variety of cultural and historical contexts. Students study how gender and sexuality intersect with other categories of identity, such as race, ethnicity, class, disability, and nationality. Our curriculum prepares students to be leaders in the community, providing them with the necessary tools to navigate an increasingly global world. Gender and women’s studies (GWS) provides students with a high degree of flexibility in choosing their courses while also ensuring that they understand the foundations of the field and its core themes. Students learn to think critically, to work across disciplines, and to approach social problems in a multifaceted way. Many of our students are double majors, combining their interest in GWS with other fields such as nursing, social work, history, biology, sociology, political science, psychology, or world languages. Graduates go on to pursue careers in such areas as law, medicine, public policy, social work, teaching, non-profit management, business, and many others.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Genetics and Genomics
Requirements: To declare this major, students must be admitted to UW–Madison and the College of Agricultural and Life Sciences (CALS). All students who are admitted to CALS may declare the Genetics and Genomics major. For information about undergraduate admission to the university, see the Office of Admissions and Recruitment website.
Department: College of Agricultural and Life Sciences
Description: Genetics is the study of how traits are inherited and how the information that guides the development and function of an organism is stored and transmitted between generations. Genetics is at the heart of many of the most significant advances in biology today and provides the tools and framework for our modern understanding of all of the life sciences. From new treatments for cancer and rare diseases to new ways to address climate change and increase the global food supply, genetics is at the forefront of innovation. The Genetics and Genomics program offers students a solid foundation in the principles of genetics, while also providing them with the opportunity to explore the latest developments in genomics and the many ways that genetics is being used to address global challenges. Students in the program learn about the molecular basis of inheritance, the structure and function of genomes, the genetic basis of complex traits, and the role of genetics in evolution and development. They also gain experience in the laboratory and develop skills in data analysis and critical thinking.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://guide.wisc.edu/undergraduate/agricultural-life-sciences/genetics/genetics-modern-world-certificate/

Requirements: There are no admission requirements for the Geography major. Students should meet with the undergraduate advisor to declare the major. However, students are encouraged to declare early so that they can receive advising from the geography advisor and have access to the department's resources. Students apply to the University of Wisconsin–Madison through the Office of Admissions and Recruitment. Prospective students should consult the admissions website for information about undergraduate admission.
Description: Geography is the study of the earth as the home of humanity. It is a diverse and integrative discipline that bridges the physical and social sciences. Geography is a spatial science that looks at the ways in which physical and human phenomena are distributed over space, why they are there, and how they interact. The geography major at UW–Madison is broad and flexible, allowing students to tailor their studies to their interests. The major includes courses in physical geography, human geography, people–environment geography, and cartography and geographic information systems (GIS). Students can choose to focus their studies in one of these areas or take a broad approach that covers multiple areas.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://guide.wisc.edu/undergraduate/letters-science/geography/geography-ba/
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, Need-based, and Departmental awards (e.g., Trewartha, Petchenik Awards)

Requirements: To declare the Geography major, a student must have a grade of C or better in one Geography course. Students must complete 120 total credits to graduate, including 30 credits in the major. The program requires completion of University General Education requirements and College of Letters & Science Breadth and Bachelor of Science requirements, which include specific math and science coursework. A minimum 2.000 GPA is required in major and upper-level coursework.
Description: Geography is the study of the Earth’s systems and the interactions between people and their environments. Geographers investigate the processes that shape the Earth’s surface, the ways that humans use and perceive the landscape, and the patterns of human activity across space and time. Geography is a diverse field that includes both the physical and social sciences, as well as the humanities. The Geography major provides students with a broad foundation in the discipline and the opportunity to specialize in one of several areas: physical geography, human geography, people–environment geography, or cartography and GIS. Students in the major develop skills in critical thinking, spatial analysis, and communication that prepare them for a wide range of careers in government, business, and non-profit organizations.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://guide.wisc.edu/undergraduate/letters-science/geography/geography-bs/geography-bs_requirementstext.pdf

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Geology and Geophysics
Requirements: Students may declare the geosciences major after they have completed at least one GEOSCI course (other than GEOSCI 115) with a grade of C or better. For general undergraduate admission, applicants must provide official high school transcripts and complete two required essays as part of the application process. The university uses a holistic review process that includes academic performance, essays, and extracurricular activities. ACT or SAT scores are optional for applicants through the Spring 2025 term.
Concentration: Geology, Geophysics, Environmental Geology, General Geology
Description: Geology and geophysics is the study of the Earth, including its composition, structure, physical properties, and history. Because the geosciences are a synthesis of other sciences, students in geology and geophysics also study mathematics, physics, chemistry, and biology. Geoscientists explore for natural resources (such as minerals, oil, and gas), manage water resources, and solve environmental problems. They also study natural hazards such as earthquakes, volcanoes, and landslides. The program in geology and geophysics provides students with a solid foundation in the geosciences and prepares them for a variety of careers in industry, government, and education, as well as for graduate study.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Geology and Geophysics
Requirements: General undergraduate application requirements for the University of Wisconsin-Madison include a completed application (Common App or UW System App), two required essays, official high school transcripts, and one letter of recommendation. UW–Madison is test-optional for the ACT and SAT. To declare the Bachelor of Science in Geology and Geophysics specifically, students must first be admitted to the university and then may declare the major after completing any GEOSCI course (except GEOSCI 106, 109, 140, 190, 198, 199, 299, 431, 444, 455, 456, 457) with a grade of C or better.
Description: Geoscience is a multi-disciplinary field that studies the features, processes and history of the earth, other planets, and their moons. Geoscience involves the study of the solid earth and its atmosphere, oceans, and biosphere. By understanding the earth’s history, geoscientists are better able to predict future changes in the environment. Many geoscientists work to solve problems related to earth resources, environmental protection, and natural hazards such as earthquakes, floods, and landslides.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://partner.studymetro.com/s/course-session/a0C2x00000POxGKEA1/pn399473

Requirements: Admission to the Bachelor of Arts in German program is handled through the University of Wisconsin–Madison's Office of Admissions and Recruitment. Applicants must submit a completed application (Common App or UW System Application), two required essays, and official high school transcripts. The admissions process is holistic, considering academic rigor, grades, and non-academic factors such as leadership, service, and extracurricular activities. Students may declare the German major at any time once admitted to the university.
Description: German is the native language of some 100 million people. It is the most widely spoken first language in the European Union, and one of the world's most important languages of commerce and technology. German culture has for centuries been at the core of the humanities in the West. It is the language of Goethe, Kafka, and Brecht; of Luther, Freud, and Marx; of Mozart, Beethoven, and Wagner; and of Kant, Nietzsche, and Heidegger. UW–Madison's German program is one of the largest and strongest in the United States. Its curriculum is designed to lead students to a high level of proficiency in the language and to provide them with a deep understanding of the cultures of the German-speaking world. Students in the program explore a full range of topics, including literature and philosophy, linguistics, history and politics, film and popular culture, and more. Most of our students take advantage of the opportunity to study in Germany on one of our several study abroad programs.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

Requirements: To declare the German major, students must have completed GERMAN 204 or equivalent. Students should meet with the undergraduate advisor for German to declare the major. For admission to the University of Wisconsin–Madison, freshman applicants must submit high school transcripts, two required essays, and one letter of recommendation from a teacher or counselor. ACT or SAT scores are optional.
Description: German is the official language of Germany, Austria, and Liechtenstein, and it is one of the official languages of Switzerland and Luxembourg. It is the most widely spoken first language in the European Union and is one of the world's most important languages of business, science, and technology. The German program offers students the opportunity to learn about the language, literature, and culture of German-speaking countries. One of the largest and most consistently top-ranked programs in the United States, the German program has a world-class faculty with expertise in areas ranging from linguistics to literature to culture. Our students study German for many different reasons: to travel and live in German-speaking countries; to learn more about their own heritage; to prepare for graduate study in German or other fields; or to broaden their intellectual horizons and develop their communicative skills.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Global Health
Requirements: To declare this major, students must be admitted to UW–Madison and the College of Agricultural and Life Sciences (CALS). All students are eligible to declare Global Health. For more information, please contact the program advisor.
Department: College of Agricultural and Life Sciences
Description: The undergraduate certificate in Global Health provides students with a holistic framework for understanding the factors that influence health and disease at the local, national, and international levels. Through a combination of core courses, electives, and a global health-related field experience, students examine the biological, social, cultural, and environmental determinants of health and explore the impact of globalization on health outcomes. The certificate is intended to complement a student’s major and provide them with the knowledge and skills needed to address complex health challenges in an increasingly interconnected world.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://guide.wisc.edu/undergraduate/agricultural-life-sciences/entomology/global-health-certificate/

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Health Promotion and Health Equity
Requirements: The Health Promotion and Health Equity (HPHE) program is an open-enrollment program for all students who are admitted to the University of Wisconsin–Madison. Students can declare the program at any time after their first semester of coursework at UW-Madison. Current students can submit a declaration form on the School of Education website. Prospective students should apply to UW–Madison through the Office of Admissions and Recruitment.
Description: The Bachelor of Science (BS) in Health Promotion and Health Equity (HPHE) program is designed for students who are interested in pursuing a career in health promotion, health equity, or a health-related field. This includes careers such as a community health specialist, public health educator, health researcher, or health policy analyst, or pursuing graduate work in medicine, physical therapy, occupational therapy, nursing, or public health. Students in the Health Promotion and Health Equity (HPHE) program develop skills to support people across the lifespan in various settings (e.g., community, workplace, school, clinical) to live their healthiest lives. These skills include learning how to assess the health needs of a community or population, create and implement health programs, and evaluate the effectiveness of these programs. The HPHE major is a collaborative program among three departments in the School of Education: Counseling Psychology, Kinesiology, and Rehabilitation Psychology and Special Education. The program is designed to provide students with a well-rounded education in health promotion and health equity by offering courses in these three departments.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://guide.wisc.edu/undergraduate/education/kinesiology/health-promotion-health-equity-bs/

Requirements: Students may declare a major in history at any time. There are no prerequisite courses required to declare the major. For more information, please see the department website or contact a history advisor.
Description: History is more than just a list of names and dates; it’s the study of the past in all its complexity. From the origins of the world’s religions to the history of video games, our courses cover it all. At UW–Madison, students learn to explore how our world has changed and how it remains the same. History students engage with people and ideas from around the world and from every era. They also learn how to use evidence to build powerful arguments, think critically, and communicate effectively. For our graduates, history is a launchpad to a successful career. Our alumni work in every field imaginable, from medicine and law to business and the non-profit sector. Because of their unique combination of skills—research, communication, and critical thinking—history majors are always in demand.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://guide.wisc.edu/undergraduate/letters-science/history/history-ba/history-ba.pdf

Requirements: To declare the History major, students must meet with a history advisor. Students may declare the major at any time; however, it is recommended that they do so as soon as possible. For more information, please see the department website.
Description: The study of history is a process of constant investigation. Historians use evidence from the past to understand the world we live in today. They study every imaginable aspect of human experience: politics and government, war and revolution, religion and culture, social life and the economy. History is a bridge between the humanities and the social sciences. It is also an incredibly flexible major that can be tailored to meet a student’s interests and goals. History majors learn to think critically, to write and speak with clarity and precision, to understand the diversity of human experience across time and space, and to evaluate various types of historical evidence. These skills are essential in any career.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://guide.wisc.edu/undergraduate/letters-science/history/history-bs/history-bs_wisconsinexperiencetext.pdf

Requirements: Admissions to the major is open to all UW–Madison undergraduate students in good academic standing. For information on how to declare the Horticulture major, please visit the Declare the Major page on the department's website. Students may declare this major at any time. The Office of Admissions and Recruitment provides information about application for students who are not currently enrolled at UW–Madison.
Department: College of Agricultural and Life Sciences
Concentration: Organic and Sustainable Agriculture; Plant Science; Food and Ornamental Horticulture; Horticulture and Business
Description: Horticulture is the science, art, and business of growing and using fruits, vegetables, flowers, and ornamental plants. The horticulture major is designed to provide students with the knowledge and skills for careers in several areas including plant science, nursery and greenhouse management, landscape design, turfgrass management, and fruit and vegetable production. Students in the horticulture major can choose from several tracks: Organic and Sustainable Agriculture; Plant Science; Food and Ornamental Horticulture; or Horticulture and Business. Each track provides a solid foundation in basic sciences and plant biology while allowing students to focus on their specific interests. Horticulturalists use their knowledge to: breed and develop new plant varieties with improved traits like disease resistance, drought tolerance, and better flavor; develop sustainable production systems for fruits and vegetables; design and manage beautiful and functional gardens, parks, and landscapes; improve the quality of the environment by using plants to clean the air and water, and to reduce soil erosion; provide fresh, healthy food for people around the world; manage turfgrass for use in golf courses, athletic fields, and home lawns. In addition to being a science and an art, horticulture is also a business. Many horticulture graduates go on to own or manage their own businesses, such as greenhouses, nurseries, and landscape companies. Others work in sales, marketing, and management for large horticulture corporations. UW–Madison horticulture graduates are in high demand by employers. The department has a long history of excellence in research, teaching, and outreach, and its graduates are well-prepared for successful careers in the horticulture industry.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://guide.wisc.edu/undergraduate/agricultural-life-sciences/plant-agroecosystem-sciences/horticulture-bs/
ScholarshipAmount: Over $1,000,000 awarded annually by the college

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Human Development and Family Studies
Requirements: UW–Madison undergraduate admission is a holistic process. Requirements include a completed application (Common App or UW System App), official high school transcripts, one required essay (statement of purpose), and a list of extracurricular activities. Standardized test scores (ACT or SAT) are optional through the spring 2025 term. For students already enrolled at UW-Madison, they may declare the Human Development and Family Studies major once they have reached sophomore standing (24 credits).
Description: The Human Development and Family Studies (HDFS) major focuses on the study of people and families. It is an interdisciplinary program that examines the psychological, social, and biological aspects of human development across the lifespan, and the ways in which families and other social contexts influence that development. Students in the HDFS major gain a deep understanding of how individuals and families grow, change, and interact with one another and their communities. They also learn how to apply this knowledge to improve the lives of individuals and families through research, policy, and practice. The HDFS major is an excellent choice for students who are interested in careers in human services, education, health care, law, or public policy. It also provides a strong foundation for graduate study in a variety of fields, including psychology, sociology, social work, and human development and family studies.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).
Accredidation: The Human Development and Family Studies (HDFS) major curriculum has been approved by the National Council on Family Relations (NCFR) for the Certified Family Life Educator (CFLE) designation.
ScholarshipAmount: Over $1,000,000 total awarded by the School of Human Ecology annually

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Individual Major
Requirements: Students may apply for the Individual Major after they have completed at least 30, but no more than 75, degree credits. Students must have at least a 2.000 cumulative GPA. The application includes: a written proposal, including a list of courses, explaining the student's reasons for wanting an individual major; a faculty committee of three members from at least two UW–Madison departments who will support the student's individual major proposal; a list of courses that will make up the major. Students should meet with the Individual Major coordinator in L&S Academic Advising Services to discuss the proposed major and the application process.
Description: The individual major provides a student with the opportunity to design a major when their academic interests are not fully met by any of the existing majors at the University of Wisconsin–Madison. This program is intended for students who have a focused area of study that is interdisciplinary in nature and cannot be met by an existing major or combination of majors and certificates. To be eligible for the individual major, a student must have a minimum of a 3.000 cumulative grade point average (GPA) on at least 30 credits in residence at UW–Madison. In addition, the student must have at least 30 degree credits remaining to be completed at the time the individual major is approved by the College of Letters & Science. The degree awarded is either a Bachelor of Arts (BA) or a Bachelor of Science (BS) in the Individual Major.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Individual Major
Requirements: To be eligible to apply for an individual major, students must: be in residence in the College of Letters & Science with a minimum 2.000 GPA; be at least second-semester freshmen; submit their proposal for review and receive approval before they have earned 84 credits. The proposal must include: a list of courses; a written statement of the student’s reasons for seeking an individual major, including why the proposed major is appropriate for the student’s goals and how it differs from existing majors; and a recommendation from a faculty committee of at least three members.
Description: The Individual Major is an option for students who wish to pursue a program of study that is not available through an established major. Each student works with a faculty committee to design a major that is built around a coherent theme. The individual major must be significantly different from any existing major and must be interdisciplinary in nature. The major must be approved by the College of Letters & Science Faculty Committee on Individual Majors.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Industrial Engineering
Requirements: To be considered for admission to the Bachelor of Science in Industrial Engineering, applicants must submit a complete application via the Common App or UW System Application. Required materials include official high school transcripts and two application essays. While not required, one letter of recommendation is encouraged. For the College of Engineering specifically, it is expected that applicants have completed 4 units of math (including calculus if available), 1 unit of chemistry, and 1 unit of physics. Direct admission to the major is competitive and based on a holistic review of the applicant's academic record and extracurricular involvement.
Description: Industrial engineers (IEs) are the only engineers trained to be specialists in productivity and quality improvement. IEs are people-oriented, and they enjoy the challenge of solving problems in many different environments. In addition to traditional manufacturing, industrial engineers work in such areas as healthcare, transportation, banking, insurance, and communication. Industrial engineers examine how to best use the resources available to provide a service or manufacture a product. This may involve the study of people, equipment, materials, and information. The industrial engineer makes sure that people have the best tools, workstation, and work environment to do their job. IEs also design the flow of work and the interaction of people and machines. Students study such things as time and motion, engineering management, work-system design, information systems, human factors, and ergonomics. Industrial engineering at UW–Madison is one of the top programs in the nation.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).
Accredidation: Accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org, under the commission’s General Criteria and the Program Criteria for Industrial and Similarly Named Engineering Programs.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Business Administration in Information Systems
Requirements: Admissions to the Information Systems major is a two-step process. First, students must be admitted to the Wisconsin School of Business. Second, students must meet with an academic advisor. Requirements to be admitted to the Wisconsin School of Business vary based on a student’s current status (prospective student, current UW–Madison student, or transfer student). See the School of Business undergraduate admissions page for more information.
Description: Businesses rely on information systems to function and compete in today’s economy. The Information Systems (IS) major prepares students for positions as IS professionals or for work in other functional areas where an understanding of information systems is essential. The IS major provides students with the technical, interpersonal, and business skills required to succeed in a variety of business-technology roles. Students explore how IS can provide value by improving business processes and providing better information for decision-making. Information systems are designed to help organizations reach their goals, and IS professionals design and implement these systems.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://guide.wisc.edu/undergraduate/business/accounting-information-systems/

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Interior Architecture
Requirements: Admission to the Interior Architecture major is a two-part process. All students are admitted to the Bachelor of Science in Interior Architecture. Students must complete a set of prerequisite courses and a portfolio for the Creative Arts practice to move into the professional sequence (junior and senior years). All students must apply to the professional sequence. Students apply for the professional sequence in the spring of their sophomore year (or second year at UW–Madison). Admission to the professional sequence is competitive and based on a portfolio review. A minimum GPA of 2.75 is required. General university freshman admission requires a completed application, official high school transcripts, and one essay. ACT or SAT scores and a letter of recommendation are optional.
Description: Interior architecture is a professional program that explores the relationship between human behavior and the environment. Designers find creative solutions for the spaces in which people live and work. They strive to improve the health, safety, and welfare of the public and to enhance the quality of life. The professional curriculum includes courses in hand drawing, CAD, 3D modeling, lighting, materials, color, building systems, and sustainable design. Professional practice, design for a variety of users, and space planning are also taught. Interior Architecture students work closely with design professors in a studio setting.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).
Accredidation: The Interior Architecture program is accredited by the Council for Interior Design Accreditation (CIDA) and the National Association of Schools of Art and Design (NASAD).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Business Administration in International Business
Requirements: The International Business major must be taken as a second major; it cannot be the first or only major. Admission to the Wisconsin School of Business is required.
