Students are admitted to the school through either the Direct Admit (freshman) process or the Pre-Business (current UW–Madison student) application process. The application process for the Wisconsin School of Business typically requires a personal statement (essay) and a resume. Additionally, students must complete specific prerequisite coursework and meet credit requirements as part of the broader BBA program.
Description: International business is a second major that provides students with the opportunity to gain a broader global perspective. Students will learn the significance of various global issues such as world trade, international management, and global marketing. The program’s mission is to offer a comprehensive, multidisciplinary curriculum that will help students think globally and prepare them for a variety of international careers. The international business major must be taken in conjunction with another business major. Students may not double major in international business and business: health care management.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://guide.wisc.edu/undergraduate/business/

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in International Studies
DeadlineDate: Early Action: November 1; Regular Decision: February 1
Requirements: There are no prerequisites for declaring the International Studies major. Students are encouraged to declare as soon as they decide on the major. Students must meet with the International Studies advisor to declare the major.
Concentration: Global Economy, Global Security, Culture in the Age of Globalization
Description: The International Studies Major (IS Major) is an interdisciplinary program that allows students to study the world’s most pressing problems from a variety of perspectives. Students take courses in the social sciences, humanities, and professional schools to gain a broad understanding of international issues and then specialize in one of three thematic options: Global Economy, Global Security, or Culture in the Age of Globalization. The IS Major provides students with the tools to understand the complex interactions between states, non-state actors, and individuals in the global arena.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://guide.wisc.edu/undergraduate/letters-science/institute-regional-international-studies/international-studies-bs/international-studies-bs.pdf

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in International Studies
Requirements: To declare the major, students must schedule an appointment with an International Studies advisor. Students must also complete a brief online information session (as of June 2021).
Concentration: Global Security, Global Economy, or Culture in the Age of Globalization
Description: International Studies (IS) is a multidisciplinary major that allows students to explore how global processes—be they economic, political, or cultural—interact with each other and with specific places around the world. The major is designed to provide students with a broad and rigorous foundation for understanding the complex issues that characterize our modern world. In addition to a core set of courses in international studies, students choose a track (option) in one of three areas: Global Security, Global Economy, or Culture in the Age of Globalization. Students also take courses that focus on a specific region of the world (e.g., Africa, Asia, Europe, Latin America, Middle East, Russia/Central Eurasia). To gain further depth, students must complete at least five semesters of a single foreign language. As a result of this training, IS majors are prepared for a range of careers in both the public and private sectors, including government, international organizations, business, and non-profit organizations.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://guide.wisc.edu/undergraduate/letters-science/institute-regional-international-studies/international-studies-bs/

Requirements: Students may declare the Italian major at any time. For more information, please visit the Italian major page or see the French and Italian Undergraduate Advisor.
Description: Italian at UW–Madison is a vibrant, well-rounded program that offers students a great deal of flexibility. Students who major in Italian will gain a high level of language proficiency and an in-depth understanding of Italian culture. We offer courses on topics as diverse as Italian cuisine, cinema, comics and graphic novels, the Renaissance, and opera. Our students also study the work of many major figures of Italian literature such as Dante, Machiavelli, and Elena Ferrante. Students can take most of these courses in Italian or in English. Students may choose to focus more on language and culture or on literature. To gain even more proficiency, many Italian majors spend a summer, a semester, or a year studying in Italy through one of the university’s many study abroad programs. Students who study Italian find that their language and culture skills make them strong candidates for a variety of careers in fields such as business, law, fashion, the food and beverage industry, design, education, and international relations.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://guide.wisc.edu/undergraduate/letters-science/french-italian/italian-ba/

Requirements: Admission to the Bachelor of Science in Italian is through the general University of Wisconsin–Madison undergraduate admission process. There are no additional admission requirements for this major; students may declare the Italian major at any time. The university application requires high school transcripts, two essays, and one letter of recommendation. A holistic review process is used, considering academic excellence (typically 4 units of English, 4 units of math, 3-4 units of social studies, 3-4 units of science, and 2 units of a single world language) as well as non-academic factors like leadership, service, and extracurricular activities.
Description: The Department of French and Italian offers students a wealth of opportunities for the study of the languages and cultures of France, Italy, and other countries where French or Italian is spoken. Our students explore the literature and culture of these countries from the Middle Ages to the present day. Students can also study Italian and French for business and take courses in cinema and media studies, gender and women's studies, second language acquisition, and food studies. In all of our programs, students develop communicative and cultural competency as well as strong analytical and critical thinking skills. Our majors find careers in a wide range of fields including business, law, international relations, education, journalism, non-profit management, and public policy.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

Requirements: To apply for undergraduate admission to the University of Wisconsin–Madison, applicants must submit a completed application (via the Common App or UW System Application), two essays, official high school transcripts, and at least one letter of recommendation. For the Japanese major specifically, students are admitted to the university first and can then declare the major through the Department of Asian Languages and Cultures. There are no additional admission requirements to declare the Japanese major beyond being an admitted student in the College of Letters & Science.
Description: Japanese is one of the world's major languages. In addition to being spoken by the 127 million people who live in Japan, it is also used as a second language by people in Chinese and Korean communities and other parts of Asia. Knowledge of Japanese is becoming more and more important as Japan's role as a major economic power and its importance in international politics increases. The undergraduate major in Japanese is designed to provide students with proficiency in the Japanese language and a solid foundation in Japanese literature and culture. It is intended both for students who wish to pursue a career in such fields as business, government, or journalism, and for those who intend to go on to graduate study in Japanese literature or linguistics.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

Requirements: To be admitted to the University of Wisconsin–Madison, students must complete a rigorous high school curriculum including: 4 units of English, 4 units of mathematics, 3-4 units of social studies, 3-4 units of science, and at least 2 units of a single world language. For the Japanese major specifically, students may declare the major at any time by scheduling an appointment with the undergraduate advisor. There are no additional admission requirements for the Japanese BS beyond admission to the College of Letters & Science.
Description: The Department of Asian Languages and Cultures (ALC) offers a wide range of courses on the languages, literatures, and cultures of East, South, and Southeast Asia. ALC's undergraduate programs are designed to provide students with a well-rounded education in the traditions and contemporary developments of these regions. The department offers three undergraduate majors: Chinese, Japanese, and Languages and Cultures of Asia. The Japanese major provides students with a high level of proficiency in Japanese language and a deep understanding of Japanese culture, literature, and history. Students in the Japanese major develop skills in critical thinking, cross-cultural communication, and linguistic analysis.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

ProgramName: Journalism Bachelor of Arts in Journalism
Requirements: Admission to the School of Journalism and Mass Communication is competitive. Students may apply to the School of Journalism and Mass Communication after they have completed at least 24 degree credits or are currently enrolled in JOURN 201 Introduction to Mass Communication. Students must complete JOURN 201 with a grade of C or better to be eligible for admission. Admission is based on students' grade point average and a written personal statement.
Description: The School of Journalism and Mass Communication (SJMC) provides a professional education within the context of the liberal arts. The school’s curriculum is designed to help students learn how to gather, write, edit, and disseminate information and messages for a variety of audiences across a range of channels. Students choose from two tracks: the reporting track (for students interested in careers in news and information, whether for print, broadcast, or multimedia) and the strategic communication track (for students interested in careers in advertising, public relations, and integrated marketing communications). Regardless of track, SJMC students are expected to have a broad background in the liberal arts and to develop a deep understanding of the legal, ethical, and social roles of the media.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://guide.wisc.edu/undergraduate/letters-science/journalism-mass-communication/journalism-mass-communication-jba/journalism-mass-communication-jba.pdf
Accredidation: The school is one of about 100 programs across the country accredited by the Accrediting Council on Education in Journalism and Mass Communications (ACEJMC).

ProgramName: Journalism Bachelor of Science in Journalism
Requirements: Admission to the school is based on a separate application. Students are eligible to apply when they have completed 24 or more credits and have completed or are currently enrolled in JOURN 201 with a grade of C or better. Selection is based on the student's personal statement, grade point average, and evidence of academic and/or professional potential.
Concentration: Journalism (the news and information track) or Strategic Communication
Description: The School of Journalism and Mass Communication (SJMC) is a professional school within the College of Letters & Science. Our undergraduate program is designed to provide students with a well-rounded liberal arts education along with professional training in journalism and mass communication. We prepare students for careers in news and information, and strategic communication. SJMC students may choose to follow one of two tracks: Journalism (the news and information track) or Strategic Communication.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://guide.wisc.edu/undergraduate/letters-science/journalism-mass-communication/journalism-mass-communication-jbs/journalism-mass-communication-jbs.pdf
Accredidation: The School of Journalism and Mass Communication is accredited by the Accrediting Council on Education in Journalism and Mass Communications (ACEJMC).

Requirements: Admission to the professional program in Kinesiology is a competitive process. Applicants must meet the following requirements: completion of at least 40 college-level credits by the end of the application semester; a minimum cumulative GPA of 2.75 based on all college-level coursework; and completion of specific prerequisite courses including General Chemistry, Biology (or Zoology), Anatomy, Physiology, and Physics with a grade of C or better. Applicants must submit a personal statement (approximately 500 words) as part of their application to the professional program.
Description: The Kinesiology undergraduate program is designed to provide students with a well-rounded foundation in the human movement sciences. The program focuses on the biological and behavioral aspects of movement. Students take a core of foundation courses, including anatomy, physiology, biomechanics, exercise physiology, motor learning and control, and the psychology and sociology of physical activity. This broad foundation prepares students for a wide range of careers in health and fitness, as well as for further study in graduate or professional programs, such as physical therapy, occupational therapy, medicine, and other health-related fields.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

Requirements: Admissions to the BLA major are through a competitive application process. All students interested in the BLA major must first be admitted to UW–Madison. Requirements for the major application include: a BLA Application Form, a one-page Statement of Interest, a Portfolio of work, and unofficial transcripts.
Description: The Bachelor of Landscape Architecture (BLA) program at the University of Wisconsin-Madison is a professional degree program that prepares students for the practice of landscape architecture. The program focuses on the design, planning, and management of the land to create sustainable and resilient communities and environments. Students in the BLA program learn how to analyze, design, and manage natural and built environments through a curriculum that integrates design studio, ecology, technology, and professional practice.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://dpla.wisc.edu/https-dpla-wisc-edu-academics-bla-public-information/
Accredidation: Accredited by the Landscape Architectural Accreditation Board (LAAB)

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Landscape Architecture
Requirements: The Bachelor of Science–Landscape Architecture (BSLA) is a professional program. Students intending to major in landscape architecture typically enter UW–Madison as Landscape Architecture 'pre-majors' (LAA). Formal application to the professional landscape architecture major occurs during the spring semester of the first year of the pre-major, usually in February. To be eligible for the professional program, students must have completed or be currently enrolled in LAND ARC 211 (Design and Graphic Communication) and LAND ARC 250 (Survey of Landscape Architecture Design). The application requires a one-page statement of interest explaining why the student wants to pursue a degree in landscape architecture and an unofficial transcript. Admission is competitive and based on the student’s performance in the prerequisite courses, overall academic record, and the quality of the statement of interest.
Department: College of Agricultural and Life Sciences
Description: Landscape architecture is the design and stewardship of the land. It is a profession that combines art and science to create places for people while protecting and restoring the environment. Landscape architects work on a wide variety of projects, from small urban gardens to large-scale regional plans. The Bachelor of Science–Landscape Architecture (BSLA) is a professional degree program. Students take a sequence of studio courses that develop the design, technical, and communication skills of the landscape architect. The program is accredited by the Landscape Architectural Accreditation Board (LAAB). This accreditation ensures that the program meets the standards of the profession and prepares students for licensure. Students in the BSLA program learn to use a variety of tools and techniques to design and communicate their ideas. They also learn about the history and theory of landscape architecture, as well as the environmental and social factors that influence the design process. The program culminates in a senior capstone project, where students have the opportunity to apply their knowledge and skills to a real-world design project.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).
Accredidation: Accredited by the Landscape Architectural Accreditation Board (LAAB)

Requirements: To apply for undergraduate admission to the University of Wisconsin–Madison (including for the Bachelor of Arts in Latin), applicants must submit the Common Application. The holistic review process includes an evaluation of academic performance (rigor of coursework, GPA, and class rank), application essays, one required letter of recommendation (up to two accepted), and extracurricular activities. For the Latin major specifically, students generally declare the major after completing LATIN 104 or equivalent and meeting with the department advisor.
Description: The Latin major is designed to provide students with a high level of proficiency in the Latin language, a good knowledge of the literature, and a broad understanding of the Roman world. Students who complete the major will have a solid understanding of the Latin language and its literature, and will be able to read and analyze a wide variety of texts. The major also provides an excellent foundation for graduate study in classics, archaeology, ancient history, and other related fields. Students learn to: apply the concepts of grammar, syntax, and morphology to the translation of Latin texts; analyze the formal and thematic features of Latin literature in its historical and cultural context; evaluate the reception and influence of Latin literature and Roman culture on subsequent periods and cultures; and produce clear and effective writing and research on topics related to Latin literature and Roman culture.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

Requirements: To be admitted to the University of Wisconsin–Madison, students must have completed the following high school coursework: 4 units of English, 4 units of mathematics, 3–4 units of social science, 3–4 units of science, and 2–4 units of a single world language. There are no additional admission requirements for the Latin major. To declare the Latin major, students must meet with the undergraduate advisor in the department.
Description: The department offers two undergraduate majors: Latin and Classics. Students who choose the Latin major study the language, literature, and culture of the Roman world. Latin is the language of the Roman Empire and the common language of intellectual, legal, and religious life in Europe through the Middle Ages and into the early modern period. Students who major in Latin gain a deep understanding of the language, literature, and history of Rome and its influence on later cultures. Latin students develop strong analytical and communication skills that are valuable for careers in many fields, including education, law, medicine, and business. Many Latin majors also choose to double major in other subjects, such as History, Art History, or Philosophy.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Latin American, Caribbean and Iberian Studies
Requirements: To apply for the Bachelor of Arts in Latin American, Caribbean and Iberian Studies, applicants must first be admitted to the University of Wisconsin–Madison. The general application requirements include high school transcripts, two essays, and one letter of recommendation (which is optional). UW–Madison is ACT/SAT test-optional through the Spring 2025 term. There are no additional or special requirements for students to declare the Latin American, Caribbean and Iberian Studies major beyond admission to the university.
Description: Latin American, Caribbean, and Iberian Studies (LACIS) is an interdisciplinary program that offers an undergraduate major and a certificate. The program is designed to provide students with a broad, interdisciplinary understanding of the history, politics, societies, and cultures of Latin America, the Caribbean, and the Iberian Peninsula. LACIS majors and certificate students are encouraged to participate in study abroad programs in Latin America, the Caribbean, Spain, or Portugal, and to seek out internships that allow them to apply their knowledge in a professional setting. The major is designed to provide students with a strong foundation for a variety of careers, including international business, government service, non-profit organizations, and education. It also provides an excellent background for graduate study in a variety of fields, including history, political science, sociology, anthropology, and literature.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://www.globalreach.in/course-details.php?institute_course_id=NjEyNjk%3D

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Latin American, Caribbean and Iberian Studies
Requirements: Students may declare the major at any time by meeting with the LACIS undergraduate advisor. To declare, students should schedule an appointment with the advisor. The Bachelor of Science degree requires specific coursework including 6 credits of Mathematics/Computer Science/Statistics at the Intermediate or Advanced level, and a minimum of 6 credits in Natural Science.
Description: Latin American, Caribbean and Iberian Studies (LACIS) is an interdisciplinary program that provides students with a broad understanding of the history, culture, politics, and economics of Latin America, the Caribbean, Spain, and Portugal. LACIS allows students to explore these areas through a variety of lenses, including history, anthropology, political science, literature, art history, and more. Drawing on more than 100 faculty from 40 departments across the university, LACIS offers an undergraduate major and minor, a graduate certificate, and a master’s degree. Students in the major develop proficiency in Spanish or Portuguese and gain a deep understanding of the diverse regions that comprise the Iberian Peninsula and the Americas.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://iris.wisc.edu/latin-american-caribbean-and-iberian-studies/

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Legal Studies
Requirements: There are no requirements to declare the legal studies major. Students should meet with the legal studies advisor to discuss the requirements and to declare. To be admitted to the University of Wisconsin–Madison, applicants must submit an application, high school transcripts, and two essays. Test scores (ACT/SAT) are currently optional.
Description: The Legal Studies major is designed to provide a liberal arts education for students who wish to study law and its relationship to society, and who may or may not be considering a career in the legal profession. As an interdisciplinary major, Legal Studies is composed of several themes: legal institutions; law and social forces; law and culture; and law and theory. The program focuses on law and its relationship to society, rather than on the practice of law.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Legal Studies
Requirements: There are no requirements to declare the Legal Studies major. Students can declare the major via a scheduled appointment with a Legal Studies academic advisor.
Description: Legal studies is an interdisciplinary major that provides an opportunity for students to study law and legal institutions in their social, economic, and political contexts. The program is designed to provide students with a broad education in the liberal arts and sciences. It is not a professional program or a pre-law program. The major is designed to help students understand how law works in society and how society works in law. The curriculum is organized around five themes: legal institutions; processes of legal order and disorder; law and social forces; law and culture; and law and theory. The major is housed in the Center for Law, Society & Justice. Legal studies is a well-established discipline within the liberal arts. Many of the most important thinkers in the development of Western and non-Western thought have grappled with the role of law in society. The legal studies major offers students the opportunity to learn from faculty members from across the campus who bring their own disciplinary perspectives to the study of law. The program also offers a wide range of internship and other learning opportunities beyond the classroom.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://guide.wisc.edu/undergraduate/letters-science/center-law-society-justice/legal-studies-bs/

Requirements: There are no prerequisites for declaring the Linguistics major. Students may declare the major at any time. To declare the major, students should meet with the linguistics undergraduate advisor.
Description: Linguistics is the scientific study of human language. It seeks to discover the principles that underlie the structure and use of all languages. Linguists investigate a wide range of questions: How do the sounds of a language relate to its meanings? How does language change over time? What is the relationship between language and the brain? How does language vary from one social group to another? What are the commonalities between all languages? What can language tell us about human nature? Students who major in linguistics learn how to analyze the structure of language, how language is used in social contexts, and how language is processed in the brain. They also develop strong analytical and problem-solving skills that are valuable in a variety of careers.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://guide.wisc.edu/undergraduate/letters-science/language-sciences/linguistics-bs/linguistics-bs.pdf

Requirements: To apply for the Bachelor of Science in Linguistics, applicants must first be admitted to the University of Wisconsin-Madison. General undergraduate application requirements include high school transcripts, two essays, and an application fee. Letters of recommendation are optional. Once enrolled at the university, students must meet with the undergraduate advisor to declare the Linguistics major; there are no specific prerequisite courses or GPA requirements for declaration.
Description: Linguistics is the scientific study of human language. It is a wide-ranging field that includes the study of language structure (grammar), language meaning (semantics and pragmatics), language sounds (phonetics and phonology), and how these things change over time. It also includes the study of how people learn languages (language acquisition), how language is used in social contexts (sociolinguistics), and how it is processed in the brain (psycholinguistics and neurolinguistics). Linguists are interested in identifying the properties that all languages share and the ways in which they differ. They also want to understand the nature of the human capacity for language and how it interacts with other aspects of cognition. The undergraduate major in linguistics at UW–Madison provides a solid foundation in the core areas of linguistic analysis, as well as the opportunity to explore more specialized areas of the field. Students learn to analyze language data from a wide variety of languages and to think critically about the nature of language and its role in human life.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Business Administration in Management and Human Resources
Requirements: Admissions to the Wisconsin School of Business is a separate process from admission to UW–Madison. Students can apply to the Wisconsin School of Business directly from high school or as a current UW–Madison student or transfer student. For more information, please visit the School of Business website.
Description: The management and human resources major offers two distinct options: Human Resources or Management. The human resources option focuses on the people side of business, including staff recruitment and selection, performance management, employee relations, diversity and inclusion, and compensation and benefits. The management option focuses on the broader set of leadership and managerial skills needed to be successful in any organization. Students learn about organizational behavior, leadership, strategy, entrepreneurship, and innovation. The management and human resources major provides students with the knowledge and skills necessary to be effective leaders and managers in a variety of organizational settings.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://guide.wisc.edu/undergraduate/business/management-human-resources/business-administration-human-resources-bba/

ProgramName: Bachelor of Business Administration in Marketing
Requirements: Admission to the Bachelor of Business Administration (BBA) in Marketing is handled through the Wisconsin School of Business undergraduate admissions process. Applicants are evaluated based on a holistic review that includes academic achievement, a required application essay, and extracurricular involvement (leadership, service, and work experience). Freshman applicants apply via the Common Application or the UW System Application. Current UW–Madison students must complete specific prerequisite courses, including Economics, Psychology, Communication Part A, and Quantitative Reasoning Part A, prior to applying for internal admission. The university is currently test-optional for undergraduate applicants.
Description: Marketing involves the activities that guide the flow of goods and services from producer to consumer. These activities include marketing research, product planning, pricing, advertising, personal selling, physical distribution, and other functions. Marketing is an essential function in any organization, for-profit or nonprofit, and is becoming more important in today’s global and highly competitive environment.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).
Accredidation: The Wisconsin School of Business is accredited by AACSB International—The Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Materials Science and Engineering
Requirements: The College of Engineering admits students as freshmen (Direct Admission) or through a competitive application process for students already on campus (Cross-Campus Admission). Freshmen apply through the Office of Admissions and Recruitment. The program requires a total of 128 credits, including 16 credits of Liberal Studies, 15-17 credits of Mathematics (including Calculus and Differential Equations), 13-15 credits of Science (including Chemistry and Physics), and specific Materials Science and Engineering core courses. Students must maintain a minimum cumulative GPA of 2.000.
Description: Materials science and engineering (MS&E) is a field that involves the discovery and design of new materials, with a focus on solids. Materials scientists and engineers study the relationships between the structure of materials at atomic or molecular scales and their macroscopic properties. Based on this understanding, they design and manufacture materials to meet specific requirements for applications in various fields such as electronics, energy, healthcare, and transportation. The materials science and engineering program at UW–Madison is designed to provide students with a strong foundation in the physical and engineering sciences. The curriculum emphasizes the fundamental principles of thermodynamics, kinetics, and structure-property relationships, while also providing hands-on experience in materials characterization and processing. This foundation is designed to prepare students for a wide range of career opportunities in industries such as aerospace, automotive, electronics, energy, and healthcare, as well as for further study in graduate school.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://guide.wisc.edu/undergraduate/engineering/materials-science-engineering/materials-science-engineering-bs/materials-science-engineering-bs_requirementstext.pdf
Accredidation: The Bachelor of Science in Materials Science and Engineering program at the University of Wisconsin–Madison is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org, under the commission’s General Criteria and Program Criteria for Materials, Metallurgical, Ceramics and Similarly Named Engineering Programs.

Requirements: To declare the major in Mathematics, a student must have completed: MATH 221 Calculus and Analytic Geometry 1, MATH 222 Calculus and Analytic Geometry 2, or MATH 276 Modern Differential and Integral Calculus. At least one of these math courses must be taken in residence at UW–Madison. A student must also have at least a 2.000 GPA on all MATH courses taken on the UW–Madison campus.
Description: Mathematics is a science and an art. It is the study of patterns, structures, and relationships. It is a language that allows us to describe and understand the world around us. The Department of Mathematics at the University of Wisconsin–Madison is a world leader in mathematical research and education. Our faculty and students are involved in research that spans the entire range of mathematics, from the most abstract theoretical work to the most applied projects. A student who majors in mathematics will find that it is a discipline that is both challenging and rewarding. The mathematics major provides a solid foundation for students who are interested in pursuing a career in a wide range of fields, including finance, technology, education, and research. Our graduates are highly sought after by employers because of their strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://guide.wisc.edu/undergraduate/letters-science/mathematics/mathematics-ba/mathematics-ba_text.pdf

Requirements: To apply for the Bachelor of Science in Mathematics, students must first be admitted to the University of Wisconsin–Madison. The general undergraduate application requires a completed application form, two essays, and official high school transcripts. Once enrolled at the university, students may declare the Mathematics major after completing a three-course calculus sequence (MATH 221, MATH 222, and MATH 234, or equivalent) with a grade point average of 2.000 or better in those courses.
Concentration: Standard Mathematics, Mathematics for Secondary Education
Description: Mathematics is a multifaceted subject of great beauty and application. Mathematics provides the language and tools of analysis in the physical, biological, and social sciences; in engineering and technology; and in economics and computer science. Many of the most important developments in these fields are based on mathematical foundations. In addition, the study of mathematics provides students with a way of thinking that is characterized by rigorous logic, precise definitions, and an elegant clarity of exposition. The mathematics major at UW–Madison is a flexible program that can be tailored to meet a student’s particular interests. Students who major in mathematics may choose to focus their studies in a variety of areas including analysis, algebra, geometry, number theory, or probability and statistics. They can prepare for careers in business and industry or for teaching in secondary schools. Completion of a mathematics major also provides an excellent foundation for graduate study in mathematics or a related field, as well as for professional study in law or medicine.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Mechanical Engineering
Requirements: The University of Wisconsin–Madison reviews freshman applications through a holistic process. Applicants must submit the Common Application or the UW System Application, including official high school transcripts, two required essays, and an application fee. One letter of recommendation is optional. For the 2024 and 2025 application terms, UW–Madison is test-optional, meaning ACT and SAT scores are not required for admission. Admission to the College of Engineering and the Mechanical Engineering program is competitive and based on academic rigor, grades, and the overall strength of the application.
Description: Mechanical engineering is one of the most diverse of all engineering disciplines. Mechanical engineers design, develop, build, and test mechanical and thermal sensors and devices, including tools, engines, and machines. The mechanical engineering program at UW–Madison is known for its world-class faculty, cutting-edge research, and hands-on curriculum that prepares students for leadership in industry, government, and academia. Students learn to apply principles of mechanics, thermodynamics, fluid mechanics, heat transfer, materials science, and energy conversion to design and analyze systems.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).
Accredidation: Accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org, under the commission’s General Criteria and Program Criteria for Mechanical and Similarly Named Engineering Programs.

Requirements: To apply for the Bachelor of Science in Microbiology at the University of Wisconsin–Madison, freshman applicants must submit the Common Application, which includes two required essays. Applicants must also provide official high school transcripts and one letter of recommendation (which is optional but encouraged). The University of Wisconsin–Madison has a test-optional policy, meaning ACT and SAT scores are not required for admission. The Microbiology major is offered through both the College of Agricultural and Life Sciences and the College of Letters & Science.
Department: College of Agricultural and Life Sciences and the College of Letters & Science
Description: Microbiology is the study of microorganisms—bacteria, viruses, fungi, algae, and protozoa. These tiny life forms are critical to our world. They are the basis of the food chain, they support the life of plants and animals, and they help recycle the world's resources. Some are also the cause of major diseases, such as AIDS, tuberculosis, and many others. Microbiology is an exciting field that contributes to the areas of medicine, genetics, molecular biology, pharmacy, agriculture, and environmental science. A microbiology major prepares students for many different careers in health care, industry, research, and government. It also provides an excellent background for medical, dental, or veterinary school, and for graduate study in any of the biological sciences. The Microbiology major is offered by the Department of Bacteriology in the College of Agricultural and Life Sciences. The Department of Medical Microbiology and Immunology in the School of Medicine and Public Health also participates in the program.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Molecular and Cell Biology
Requirements: Admission to the University of Wisconsin–Madison is a holistic process. Applicants must submit a completed application via the Common Application or the UW System Application, which includes two required essays, official high school transcripts, and a list of extracurricular activities. The university is test-optional for the 2024-2025 terms. To declare the Molecular Biology major specifically, students must have completed MATH 221, and CHEM 103 and CHEM 104 (or CHEM 109) with a grade of C or better.
Description: Molecular biology is the study of the molecular basis of life. It is a rapidly growing field that has revolutionized our understanding of biology and medicine. The molecular biology major is an interdisciplinary program that draws on the expertise of faculty from across the university. The major is designed to provide students with a rigorous and broad-based education in the biological sciences, with a focus on the molecular and cellular levels. Students in the major will learn about the structure and function of biological molecules, the mechanisms of gene expression and regulation, and the molecular basis of disease. The major also provides students with the opportunity to gain research experience through independent study and honors research projects. The molecular biology major is an excellent preparation for students who wish to pursue careers in research, medicine, or biotechnology.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://guide.wisc.edu/undergraduate/undergraduate.pdf

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Molecular and Cell Biology
Requirements: There are no requirements to declare the major. Students are encouraged to declare as soon as they decide to pursue the major. Schedule an appointment with an academic advisor to declare the major.
Description: Molecular and Cell Biology (MCB) is a major that focuses on the study of molecular and cellular processes. It is a multidisciplinary field that combines genetics, biochemistry, and cell biology to understand how cells function and interact with their environment. The MCB major provides students with a strong foundation in the fundamental principles of molecular and cell biology, as well as opportunities to explore specialized areas such as developmental biology, neurobiology, and immunology. Students in the MCB major will develop critical thinking and problem-solving skills through coursework and laboratory research. They will also gain experience in communicating scientific findings to both technical and non-technical audiences. The MCB major prepares students for a variety of careers in research, medicine, biotechnology, and other fields related to the life sciences.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://guide.wisc.edu/undergraduate/letters-science/integrative-biology/molecular-cell-biology-bs/

Requirements: Entrance into the Mead Witter School of Music is by audition. All prospective students, including current UW–Madison students, must audition for admission to a degree program and/or to be awarded a music scholarship. To be considered for admission to the Mead Witter School of Music, all applicants must complete: 1) The University of Wisconsin–Madison application (Common App or UW System App), 2) A School of Music supplemental application (found within the UW–Madison application), and 3) An audition on their primary instrument or voice. Admission to the major requires a successful audition and completion of the Music Theory Placement Exam.
Description: The Bachelor of Arts in Music major provides a strong basis for the study of music within a liberal arts curriculum. Students complete the basic theory and history sequence required of all music majors and then select from a wide range of courses in music history, theory, ethnomusicology, and music and media. In the final year, students complete a senior project in musicology, music theory, or ethnomusicology. The B.A. is not a performance-based degree; students are encouraged to participate in the many Mead Witter School of Music ensembles and may take lessons (audition required) but these are not required for the degree.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://bulletins.psu.edu/undergraduate/colleges/arts-architecture/music-ba/
Accredidation: The Mead Witter School of Music is an accredited institutional member of the National Association of Schools of Music (NASM).

Requirements: All prospective students must apply to the University of Wisconsin–Madison through the Office of Admissions and Recruitment. For information on the university's application process and deadlines, see the Office of Admissions and Recruitment website. Simultaneously, students must apply to the Mead Witter School of Music for an audition. The School of Music application and audition determine a student's eligibility for the music major. New and transfer students are admitted to the music major only by audition. Students should consult the Mead Witter School of Music website for more information on the School of Music application process and audition dates.
Description: The School of Music offers the bachelor of arts (B.A.) and bachelor of science (B.S.) degrees with a major in music. These degrees are designed for students who want a strong liberal arts education, including a major in music, but who do not want the higher concentration of music courses and the performance requirements of the bachelor of music (B.M.) degree. Students in the B.A./B.S. programs may choose to complete a second major in another department in the College of Letters & Science.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://guide.wisc.edu/undergraduate/letters-science/music/
Accredidation: The Mead Witter School of Music is a fully accredited member of the National Association of Schools of Music (NASM).
ScholarshipType: Performance audition, academic achievement, and financial need

ProgramName: Bachelor of Music in Music: Education
Requirements: To be admitted to the Bachelor of Music in Music: Education, applicants must apply to the University of Wisconsin–Madison through the Office of Admissions and Recruitment and separately to the Mead Witter School of Music. Requirements include a successful performance audition on a primary instrument or voice, the submission of a School of Music application (which includes a musical resume and a personal statement), and the standard university application requirements including official transcripts and a personal essay. Admission is competitive and based on both academic and musical qualifications.
Department: College of Letters & Science (Mead Witter School of Music)
Description: The BM Music: Education major provides specialized training for students who wish to teach music in elementary or secondary schools. Students choose one of two tracks: Instrumental or Vocal. This program leads to the professional licensure required for teaching music in public schools in Wisconsin. It emphasizes the development of musicianship, teaching skills, and clinical experiences in various school settings.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).
Accredidation: The Mead Witter School of Music is an accredited institutional member of the National Association of Schools of Music (NASM). The Bachelor of Music: Music Education is approved by the Wisconsin Department of Public Instruction (DPI).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Music in Music: Performance
Requirements: All prospective students must first be admitted to the University of Wisconsin–Madison. Prospective music majors must also apply for admission to the Mead Witter School of Music and pass an audition. Specific details and information on auditions and applying to the Mead Witter School of Music can be found on the School of Music website Admissions page. Music applicants must complete the Mead Witter School of Music application and audition on their primary instrument/voice.
Description: The Mead Witter School of Music is committed to a distinctive program of musical study, which, as part of a great university, provides a dynamic environment for learning, research, and performance. Within this context, the School of Music creates a synthesis of diverse musical traditions through a curriculum that provides students with a sound basis for both professional careers and a lifetime of personal growth. To ensure this, the school provides an atmosphere that is conducive to the growth of students, not only as musicians, but also as well-rounded individuals.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://guide.wisc.edu/undergraduate/letters-science/music/music-performance-bm/music-performance-voice-bm/
Accredidation: The Mead Witter School of Music is an accredited institutional member of the National Association of Schools of Music (NASM).

Requirements: To apply for the Bachelor of Arts in Neurobiology as an undergraduate at UW-Madison, applicants must submit a completed application, two essays, official high school transcripts, and at least one letter of recommendation. Standardized test scores (ACT or SAT) are optional for students applying through the Spring 2025 term. Students already enrolled at UW–Madison may declare the major at any time by meeting with an academic advisor.
Description: Neurobiology is the study of the nervous system, which includes the brain, spinal cord, and individual nerve cells. It is an interdisciplinary field that employs tools from molecular biology, genetics, physiology, anatomy, and psychology to understand how the brain and nervous system function. The Neurobiology major at UW–Madison is designed to provide students with a strong foundation in the biological sciences while offering specialized training in the neurosciences. Students in the program explore topics ranging from the molecular and cellular basis of neural function to the complex processes underlying behavior and cognition. The major serves as excellent preparation for students interested in pursuing advanced degrees in medicine, veterinary medicine, physical therapy, and other healthcare professions, as well as graduate studies in neurobiology, psychology, and related fields.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

Requirements: To declare the Neurobiology major, students must have completed: BIOLOGY/BOTANY/ZOOLOGY 151 or BIOLOGY/ZOOLOGY 101 and BIOLOGY/ZOOLOGY 102 or BIOCORE 381. They must also have a cumulative GPA of 2.000 or higher. For general undergraduate admission to the University of Wisconsin-Madison, applicants must submit high school transcripts and two required essays. The university is currently test-optional through the Summer 2025 term.
Description: Neurobiology is the study of the nervous system: how it is built, how it works, and how it changes. It is a highly interdisciplinary field at the intersection of biology, psychology, chemistry, physics, and computer science. The neurobiology major provides a rigorous and multifaceted education in the field, with a focus on how the brain and nervous system function at levels ranging from the molecular to the behavioral. Students will gain a strong foundation in the basic sciences and then pursue more advanced coursework in neurobiology, exploring topics such as neural development, sensory and motor systems, and the neural basis of complex behaviors and diseases.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Nuclear Engineering
Requirements: Admission to the Bachelor of Science in Nuclear Engineering program is managed by the UW-Madison Office of Admissions and Recruitment. Freshman applicants must submit a complete application (Common App or UW System App), which includes two required essays and official high school transcripts. The university is test-optional through the Spring 2025 term, meaning ACT or SAT scores are not required but may be submitted. One letter of recommendation is also optional. Admission to the College of Engineering is based on a holistic review of academic and non-academic factors.
Description: Nuclear engineering is a modern and very exciting field of study. Nuclear engineers help design and operate nuclear power plants for the production of carbon-free electricity. They also apply the principles of nuclear science and engineering to other fields such as healthcare, food safety, and national security. The program is designed to provide students with a strong background in mathematics, science, and the engineering principles required to work in these fields. Students also have the opportunity to participate in research projects with faculty and staff in the department.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).
Accredidation: The Bachelor of Science in Nuclear Engineering at the University of Wisconsin–Madison is accredited by the Engineering Accreditation Commission of ABET, https://www.abet.org, under the commission’s General Criteria and the Program Criteria for Nuclear and Radiological and Similarly Named Engineering Programs.

Requirements: To be eligible to apply to the Bachelor of Science in Nursing (BSN) program, students must be on track to complete at least 30 college credits by the end of the spring semester prior to fall admission. Applicants must have a minimum cumulative GPA of at least 2.75 in all college-level coursework. Additionally, students must complete seven prerequisite courses with a grade of C or better: Chemistry (including lab), Microbiology (including lab), Human Anatomy, Human Physiology, Psychology, Sociology, and English Composition or Communication. Admission is competitive and based on academic record, personal statement essays, and a resume.
Description: The Bachelor of Science in Nursing (BSN) degree program is designed to prepare students as generalists for professional nursing practice. The curriculum provides students with a strong foundation in the liberal arts and sciences, as well as the knowledge and skills necessary to provide high-quality, patient-centered care in a variety of healthcare settings. The program emphasizes clinical judgment, leadership, and evidence-based practice. Graduates are eligible to sit for the National Council Licensure Examination for Registered Nurses (NCLEX-RN) and are prepared to pursue graduate education in nursing.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).
Accredidation: The baccalaureate degree program in nursing at the University of Wisconsin–Madison is accredited by the Commission on Collegiate Nursing Education (CCNE).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Nutritional Sciences
Requirements: Freshman and transfer students are admitted to the university and to the Nutritional Sciences program through the standard Office of Admissions and Recruitment application process. Students are admitted to the program under the 'Nutrition and Dietetics' option. Those who wish to change to the 'Pre-Health Professional' option should see their advisor.
Department: College of Agricultural and Life Sciences
Description: The Department of Nutritional Sciences is a leader in the biology of nutrition. Its mission is to improve human health through better nutrition by discovering and disseminating new knowledge. Undergraduate students in the department can choose between two Bachelor of Science degree options: Nutrition and Dietetics or Lactation and Health. The Nutrition and Dietetics option (formally known as Dietetics) provides a strong foundation in clinical and community nutrition. Students study how nutrition and health can be improved through biology, chemistry, and other sciences, as well as the social and psychological aspects of food. This option is ideal for students who want to become a registered dietitian nutritionist (RDN). For more information on the RDN pathway, see the Accreditation tab. This major also provides excellent preparation for professional or graduate study in health-related fields, such as medicine, physician assistant, physical therapy, or dentistry.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://guide.wisc.edu/undergraduate/agricultural-life-sciences/nutritional-sciences/nutritional-sciences-bs-nutrition-dietetics/
Accredidation: The Didactic Program in Dietetics (DPD) at UW-Madison is currently accredited by the Accreditation Council for Education in Nutrition and Dietetics (ACEND) of the Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics, 120 South Riverside Plaza, Suite 2190, Chicago, IL 60606-6995, 312-899-0040 ext. 5400.

ProgramName: Bachelor of Business Administration in Operations and Technology Management
Requirements: Admission to the BBA program and the Operations and Technology Management major is competitive. Students are admitted either through direct entry for first-year applicants or via an internal application for current UW-Madison students (pre-business). The application process involves a holistic review of academic records, including prerequisite coursework (e.g., communications, psychology, economics), and non-academic factors. Applicants must provide a resume and an essay as part of the application process. A minimum of 120 credits is required for the degree.
Description: Operations and technology management (OTM) is a multidisciplinary field that focuses on managing the processes that create and deliver products and services. In today’s competitive global environment, firms must have people who can effectively manage these processes and the technologies that support them. The OTM major prepares students to succeed in these roles. The OTM major is based on a set of core courses that provide students with a strong foundation in the principles of operations and technology management. These courses cover topics such as process analysis, quality management, supply chain management, and project management. In addition to the core courses, students can choose from a variety of elective courses to tailor their studies to their interests and career goals. The OTM major prepares students for a variety of careers in both the manufacturing and service sectors. Graduates of the OTM program are highly sought after by employers and find jobs in a wide range of industries, including consulting, manufacturing, logistics, healthcare, and technology.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://guide.wisc.edu/undergraduate/business/operations-information-management/business-operations-technology-management-bba/business-operations-technology-management-bba.pdf

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Personal Finance
Requirements: All students who apply to the University of Wisconsin-Madison and specify a School of Human Ecology (SoHE) major on their application will be considered for admission to SoHE. General undergraduate application requirements include high school transcripts, two essays, and optional ACT or SAT scores. Current UW–Madison students can apply to transfer into SoHE from another school or college on campus by completing an application.
Description: How can individuals and families best manage their resources to achieve financial well-being? Personal finance is a field that focuses on the financial ecosystems of individuals and families. The program integrates several disciplines—including economics, finance, sociology, psychology, and public policy—to help students understand how people make financial decisions and how those decisions affect their lives and communities. The curriculum provides students with a strong foundation in financial management, investments, insurance, retirement planning, and estate planning. It also emphasizes the development of critical thinking, communication, and problem-solving skills. Personal finance majors are prepared for a variety of careers in the financial services industry, including financial planning, wealth management, banking, insurance, and government agencies. They are also well-equipped to pursue graduate studies in fields such as law, business, and public policy. The Personal Finance major has two options: Financial Planning and Consumer Strategy. Students in the Financial Planning option complete coursework that meets the education requirements to sit for the CERTIFIED FINANCIAL PLANNER™ (CFP®) exam. Students in the Consumer Strategy option focus on the role of the consumer in the marketplace and the factors that influence consumer behavior.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Pharmaceutical Sciences
Requirements: Students are admitted to the BSPS program only for the fall term each year. Applications for admission are available starting in December of each year. The application deadline is February 1 of the spring semester prior to the intended fall start in the program. In addition to applying for the program, students must also be admitted to UW–Madison. Criteria for admission to the BSPS program include: Completion of a minimum of 54 credits by the end of the spring semester prior to the fall start in the program. Prerequisite courses must be completed for a grade of C or better. A cumulative GPA of at least 2.8 in all college-level coursework is required for admission to the program. Factors considered in the admission process include: Academic record, personal statement, extracurricular/leadership/service/work activities, and an interview.
Description: The pharmaceutical sciences are a group of interdisciplinary areas of study involved with the design, action, delivery, and disposition of drugs. The Bachelor of Science in Pharmaceutical Sciences (BSPS) major is intended for students who want to work in the pharmaceutical industry or who want to pursue graduate school in the pharmaceutical sciences. This program is not for students who want to become a pharmacist; that requires a Doctor of Pharmacy (PharmD) degree. The BSPS major is a two-year program that students enter after completing at least two years of undergraduate coursework.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://guide.wisc.edu/undergraduate/pharmacy/pharmacy/pharmaceutical-sciences-bs/

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Pharmacology and Toxicology
Requirements: The Pharmacology and Toxicology program is a two-year program for students in their third and fourth years of undergraduate study. Admission to the Pharmacology and Toxicology program is competitive. Enrollment is limited. Application materials include a cumulative GPA, a science GPA, a letter of intent, two letters of recommendation, and an interview. Successful applicants typically have a cumulative and science GPA of 3.0 or higher.
Description: Pharmacology is the study of the effects of drugs and other chemicals on living systems. It involves understanding how drugs work, how they are processed by the body, and how they can be used to treat disease. Toxicology is the study of the adverse effects of drugs and other chemicals on living systems. It involves understanding how chemicals can cause harm, how they can be detected and measured, and how their effects can be prevented or treated. The Bachelor of Science in Pharmacology and Toxicology program is an undergraduate major within the School of Pharmacy. This program provides a unique opportunity for students to study the biomedical sciences and their application to drug discovery and development. The curriculum is designed to provide students with a strong foundation in the basic sciences (biology, chemistry, physics, and math) followed by advanced coursework in pharmacology and toxicology. The program’s core courses include human physiology, biochemistry, pharmacology, and toxicology. Students also choose from a wide range of elective courses in areas such as immunology, neuroscience, and public health. In addition to coursework, students have the opportunity to participate in research with faculty in the School of Pharmacy and other departments across campus. Graduates of the program are well-prepared for a variety of careers in the pharmaceutical and biotechnology industries, government agencies, and academia. They are also well-qualified for further graduate or professional study in fields such as medicine, dentistry, pharmacy, and the biomedical sciences.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://guide.wisc.edu/undergraduate/pharmacy/pharmacy/pharmacology-toxicology-bs/

Requirements: There are no additional admission requirements for the Philosophy major. Students may declare the major by meeting with a philosophy undergraduate advisor.
Description: The Department of Philosophy offers an undergraduate major leading to the bachelor of arts or the bachelor of science degree. The department offers a wide range of courses in the main areas of philosophy, including ethics, metaphysics, epistemology, philosophy of mind, philosophy of language, philosophy of science, social and political philosophy, aesthetics, and the history of philosophy. Philosophy is the study of fundamental questions about the nature of reality, knowledge, and value. The department's courses are designed to provide students with a broad education in these areas, and to develop their abilities to think critically, write clearly, and reason logically. Philosophy is an excellent major for students who are interested in law, medicine, business, or any other field that requires the ability to analyze complex arguments and to communicate effectively.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://guide.wisc.edu/undergraduate/letters-science/philosophy/philosophy-ba/

Requirements: To declare a major in philosophy, a student must meet with the undergraduate advisor. Students should prepare for the meeting by looking over the requirements for the major, choosing a few philosophy courses that they are interested in taking, and printing out their DARS (Degree Audit Reporting System) report.
Description: Philosophy is the study of the most fundamental questions that arise in reflecting on the nature of the world and the place of human beings in it. What is the nature of reality? What can we know? What is the basis of our moral beliefs? What are the characteristics of a just society? What is the relationship between the mind and the body? Philosophy also involves the study of the methods of such inquiry. It is a discipline that emphasizes clarity of thought and expression, and the development of skills in logical analysis and the construction of sound arguments. The philosophy major at UW–Madison is designed to provide students with a broad background in the history of philosophy, as well as an introduction to the major areas of contemporary philosophy.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://guide.wisc.edu/undergraduate/letters-science/philosophy/philosophy-bs/philosophy-bs_requirementstext.pdf
ScholarshipType: Merit-based, Need-based, Departmental (e.g., Ivan Soll Prize, Benn-Hauber Scholarship)

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Physical Education
Requirements: Current UW–Madison students or students transferring from other institutions who are interested in the Bachelor of Science in Physical Education program apply to the Professional Program in Physical Education. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis. Students are generally eligible to apply when they have reached sophomore standing (24 credits) and have completed a minimum of 40 documented hours of experience working with children and/or youth in a physical activity setting. All applications will be reviewed based on the following criteria: Cumulative grade point average of at least 2.50 based on UW–Madison campus coursework, or for transfer students, their GPA from all other colleges/universities; Completed a minimum of 40 documented hours of experience working with children/youth in a physical activity setting; Personal statement; One letter of recommendation.
Description: The physical education program at UW–Madison prepares physical education teachers for certification to teach K–12 physical education (PE) and adapted physical education (APE). The curriculum focuses on developing the knowledge and skills necessary to design and implement effective physical education programs that promote physical activity and healthy lifestyles among students of all abilities. Students gain practical experience through field-based placements in local schools, starting early in the program and culminating in a semester-long student teaching experience.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://guide.wisc.edu/undergraduate/education/kinesiology/physical-education-bs/physical-education-bs_howtogetintext.pdf
Accredidation: The Physical Education program is approved by the Wisconsin Department of Public Instruction.

Requirements: The Physics Department does not have a formal application process. Students can declare the major at any time as long as they are currently enrolled in (or have completed) a physics course at UW–Madison and have a 2.500 GPA in their UW–Madison physics and math courses. To declare the major, students must make an appointment with the department’s undergraduate advisor.
Description: Physics is the study of the motion and properties of matter, the nature of space and time, and the interactions of matter and energy. It is the fundamental science and provides the basis for our understanding of the universe. The Bachelor of Arts (B.A.) or Bachelor of Science (B.S.) program in physics is intended to provide students with a solid background in the core areas of physics: classical and quantum mechanics, electromagnetism, and statistical mechanics and thermodynamics. This program is designed to prepare students for graduate study in physics or a related field, or for a wide range of careers in industry, business, or government.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://guide.wisc.edu/undergraduate/letters-science/physics/physics-ba/

Requirements: Students can declare the physics major after completing a 2-course sequence in physics (PHYSICS 247 & PHYSICS 248, PHYSICS 201 & PHYSICS 202, or PHYSICS 207 & PHYSICS 208) and a 2-course sequence in calculus (MATH 221 & MATH 222 or MATH 275 & MATH 276). To declare the physics major, students should contact a physics advisor.
Description: Physics is the study of the motion and properties of matter and energy, from the smallest subatomic particles to the largest galaxies. Physics provides the foundation for all other sciences and is a key driver of modern technology. Students in physics develop strong problem-solving and analytical skills, which are highly valued in a wide range of careers. The Department of Physics at the University of Wisconsin–Madison has a long and distinguished history of excellence in research and teaching. The department offers a wide range of courses and research opportunities for undergraduate students. Students can participate in research in many areas, including atomic, molecular, and optical physics; biophysics; condensed matter physics; high energy physics; nuclear physics; plasma physics; and quantum information and computing. The department offers the Bachelor of Arts and Bachelor of Science degrees in physics and astronomy–physics. The physics major is designed to provide students with a strong foundation in the core areas of physics, including classical mechanics, electromagnetism, quantum mechanics, and thermodynamics. The astronomy–physics major is designed for students who are interested in the study of the universe and its origins. Both majors prepare students for graduate study in physics, astronomy, or related fields, as well as for careers in industry, government, and education.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://guide.wisc.edu/undergraduate/letters-science/physics/

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Plant Pathology
Requirements: Admission to the University of Wisconsin–Madison is a prerequisite for all undergraduate majors. A complete application for freshman admission includes the Common Application, an application fee of $70, official high school transcripts, two required essays, an optional letter of recommendation, and optional standardized test scores (ACT or SAT).
Department: College of Agricultural and Life Sciences
Description: Plant pathology is the study of plant diseases, the organisms that cause them, and the ways in which they can be managed. Plant diseases are caused by a variety of organisms, including fungi, bacteria, viruses, nematodes, and parasitic plants. They can also be caused by environmental factors, such as air pollution and nutrient deficiencies. Plant pathologists use a variety of tools and techniques to study plant diseases, including microscopy, molecular biology, and field trials. They also work to develop new ways to manage plant diseases, such as through the use of resistant crop varieties, biological control agents, and pesticides. The Plant Pathology major provides students with a strong foundation in the biological and environmental sciences. Students in the major take courses in plant pathology, biology, chemistry, physics, and mathematics. They also have the opportunity to participate in research projects and internships.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

Requirements: Students may declare the Polish major at any time by contacting the undergraduate advisor. Admission to the program requires admission to the University of Wisconsin–Madison. The freshman application process requires the Common Application, high school transcripts, and two essays. Standardized test scores (ACT or SAT) and letters of recommendation are optional.
Description: With over 37 million people living in Poland and another 15-20 million living abroad, Polish is the second most widely spoken Slavic language in the world and the most widely spoken language of the European Union’s New Member States. It is a language of great history, rich literature, and vibrant culture. Historically, Poland has stood at the crossroads of European civilizations; it is now a major player in the European political and economic arena. Because of its location and its history, Poland is a key country in understanding the development of a New Europe. Studying Polish at UW–Madison is an excellent way to prepare for a wide range of careers in areas such as international business, law, and diplomacy, as well as for further study in various fields of humanities and social sciences. Many of our students choose to double-major in Polish and other fields like international studies, history, political science, or economics. The Polish major is designed to provide students with a high level of proficiency in the Polish language and a broad knowledge of Polish literature and culture. In addition to language and literature courses, students are encouraged to take courses in other departments that focus on Poland, such as history, political science, and art history.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

Requirements: To be considered for admission to the University of Wisconsin–Madison, applicants must submit the Common Application or the UW System Application, which includes a personal statement. Required materials include official high school transcripts and one letter of recommendation (optional). Applicants are expected to have completed 17 high school units, including 4 units of English, 4 of Math, 3-4 of Social Studies, 3-4 of Science, and at least 2 units of a single foreign language. For the Polish major specifically, there are no additional application requirements beyond general university admission; students typically declare the major by meeting with a program advisor.
Description: The Polish major allows students to explore the language, literature, and culture of Poland from many different perspectives. Description: Sociology is the study of social life, social change, and the social causes and consequences of human behavior. Sociologists investigate the structure of groups, organizations, and societies, and how people interact within these contexts. In fact, few fields have such broad scope and relevance for research, theory, and application of knowledge. Sociology provides many distinctive perspectives on the world, generating new ideas and critiquing the old. The field also offers a range of research techniques that can be applied to virtually any aspect of social life: street-corner interviewing, focused case studies, analysis of census-data or historical documents, laboratory experiments, and large-scale survey research.
