These students should specify Textiles & Fashion Design as their intended major on their application. Admission to the major also requires a creative portfolio review.
Description: The bachelor of science (B.S.) in textiles and fashion design (TFD) curriculum offers students a creative environment for the study of textiles and fashion design. The program's focus is on the design and making of textiles and apparel for a wide range of applications. Students learn how to integrate the elements and principles of design with an understanding of the properties and processes of materials, and to utilize a range of technologies for designing and making. Students also engage with the socio-cultural, historical, and environmental dimensions of textiles and fashion to help them develop a critical context for their own creative work. Students have access to state-of-the-art facilities, including computer-aided design labs, weaving studios, screen printing and dye labs, and apparel construction studios. The program prepares students for a diverse range of careers in the textile and fashion industries, as well as for graduate study in design and related fields.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://guide.wisc.edu/undergraduate/human-ecology/design-studies/textiles-design-certificate/
Accredidation: National Association of Schools of Art and Design (NASAD)

ProgramName: Bachelor of Arts in Theatre and Drama
Requirements: The Theatre and Drama major is an open major. Any student enrolled in the College of Letters & Science is eligible to declare. Students who reach 86 credits will need to meet with an advisor to declare the major. For more information about declaring the major, please see the department website.
Concentration: Acting Specialist; Design and Technology Specialist
Description: The Department of Theatre and Drama offers a Bachelor of Arts (B.A.) and a Bachelor of Science (B.S.) degree in theatre and drama. Our curriculum is designed to provide students with a broad base of knowledge in all areas of theatre, while also allowing for specialization in acting or design and technology. Theatre and drama is a collaborative art form. The department provides students with a comprehensive understanding of the history, theory, and practice of theatre. Students develop skills in acting, directing, design, technology, and stage management. The program prepares students for careers in professional theatre, film, television, and related fields, as well as for graduate study.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://www.wisc.edu/academics/majors/

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Theatre and Drama
Requirements: Prospective freshmen and off-campus transfer students apply to UW–Madison via the Office of Admissions and Recruitment. The application for admission also serves as the application for the Theatre and Drama major. Students intending to major in Theatre and Drama are admitted directly to the School of Education as Theatre and Drama majors. No additional application is required. Current UW–Madison students can declare the major by meeting with a Theatre and Drama advisor. Students must have a cumulative GPA of at least 2.5 on the UW–Madison campus.
Description: The Department of Theatre and Drama offers a variety of opportunities for undergraduate study. For students who choose to major in theatre and drama, two degrees are available: Bachelor of Arts (B.A.) and Bachelor of Science (B.S.). These degrees are intended for students who desire a broad liberal arts education with a major in theatre and drama. Both programs provide students with a comprehensive foundation in the history, theory, and practice of theatre. Students develop skills in creative problem-solving, collaboration, communication, and critical thinking while exploring various aspects of theatrical production, including acting, directing, design, technology, and stage management.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).
Accredidation: The Department of Theatre and Drama is a member of the National Association of Schools of Theatre (NAST).

ProgramName: Bachelor of Science in Wildlife Ecology
Requirements: Admissions to the Wildlife Ecology major are handled by the UW–Madison Office of Admissions and Recruitment. For more information, please visit the Office of Admissions website.
Department: College of Agricultural and Life Sciences
Description: The wildlife ecology major is designed for students who have a strong interest in the natural world and the conservation of biological diversity. The curriculum provides students with a solid foundation in the biological and physical sciences and focuses on the biology, ecology, and management of wild animals and the habitats they use. Students who major in wildlife ecology will be prepared for careers as professional wildlife biologists and for graduate study in the area of wildlife ecology, conservation biology, and related fields. In addition to regular coursework, students have the opportunity to participate in research projects with faculty and to work at the many state and federal natural resource agencies located in Madison. The program is certified by the Wildlife Society, and graduates are eligible for certification as Associate Wildlife Biologists.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://guide.wisc.edu/undergraduate/agricultural-life-sciences/forest-wildlife-ecology/wildlife-ecology-bs/
Accredidation: The program is certified by the Wildlife Society, and graduates are eligible for certification as Associate Wildlife Biologists.
ScholarshipType: Academic merit, financial need, and leadership

Requirements: To declare a major in Zoology, students should contact a Zoology advisor. Students may declare at any time, but are encouraged to declare early.
Description: Zoology is the study of animals: their structure, function, growth, development, reproduction, and evolution. At the University of Wisconsin–Madison, zoology is an extremely broad field, with studies ranging from the molecular level to the ecosystem level. The Department of Integrative Biology offers a wide variety of courses for majors and nonmajors. Zoology is an excellent major for students who want to explore all aspects of the animal kingdom. Because of its breadth, the major allows students to specialize in areas that interest them (e.g., cell/molecular biology, ecology, neurobiology, genetics, evolution). The zoology major is recommended for students who are interested in careers in biological and health sciences, as well as those who want to pursue graduate studies in a wide variety of biological fields. It is an excellent choice for students who plan to enter professional programs in medicine, veterinary medicine, dentistry, and other health-related fields. In addition, the major prepares students for positions in government (e.g., Department of Natural Resources, Fish and Wildlife Service), environmental organizations, and industry. Many zoology students also pursue careers in education.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://guide.wisc.edu/undergraduate/letters-science/integrative-biology/zoology-ba/

Requirements: Prospective students must apply for undergraduate admission to the University of Wisconsin–Madison through the Common Application or the UW System Application. Required materials include official high school transcripts and two essays. ACT and SAT scores are optional for the 2024-2025 and 2025-2026 application cycles. Once admitted to the university, students may declare the Zoology major at any time by making an appointment with an undergraduate advisor in the Department of Integrative Biology.
Description: Zoology is the study of animals: their structure, function, ecology, and evolution. At UW–Madison, the Zoology major is hosted by the Department of Integrative Biology. The program is designed to provide students with a broad background in the biological sciences while allowing them to focus on their specific areas of interest. The Zoology major serves as a foundation for a wide range of careers, including research, medicine and other health professions, conservation, and teaching. Many students also go on to graduate or professional school in fields such as zoology, ecology, genetics, medicine, or veterinary medicine.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

Requirements: The Accounting certificate is available only to students who are currently enrolled in the Wisconsin School of Business. Students may only declare one certificate within the School of Business. To declare the Accounting certificate, students must have completed or be currently enrolled in AIS 100 or AIS 300.
Description: The Wisconsin School of Business (WSB) provides an undergraduate certificate in accounting for non-business majors to provide students with a foundational knowledge of the language of business.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://guide.wisc.edu/undergraduate/business/business_degreesmajorscertificatestext.pdf

Requirements: All students who are not currently declared in a business major are eligible to apply for the certificate. Students who have declared a major in the Wisconsin School of Business are not eligible to complete the Accounting Fundamentals certificate. In addition to being a non-business student, admission to the certificate program is based on the following: Completion of 12 credits in residence at UW–Madison; Minimum GPA of 2.75 at UW–Madison.
Description: The Certificate in Accounting Fundamentals, offered by the Wisconsin School of Business, provides students with a strong foundation in the concepts and tools used in accounting. The certificate is designed for non-business majors to gain basic knowledge in financial and managerial accounting, as well as more specialized topics like tax and auditing. The skills learned through the certificate can be applied across many industries and roles, and can help prepare students for graduate studies in accounting or other business fields.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

Requirements: All undergraduate students in good standing at the University of Wisconsin–Madison are eligible to declare the certificate in African American Studies. To declare the certificate, students should contact the advisor. Students may not earn both the African American Studies major and the certificate.
Description: The Department of Afro-American Studies offers a program of study leading to a certificate in Afro-American studies. The certificate is intended for students who wish to emphasize Afro-American studies in their undergraduate program but do not wish to complete a full major. The certificate program allows students to develop an area of specialization in Afro-American studies and to document this on their official transcript. The Department of Afro-American Studies is a multi-disciplinary department where students can explore the history, culture, and society of Black people in the United States, the African Diaspora, and Africa. Faculty and students in the department examine the contributions of Black people to the development of modern society, the challenges they have faced, and the ways in which they have responded to those challenges.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

Requirements: To declare the African Studies Certificate, students must be a degree-seeking undergraduate student. Students are encouraged to declare as early as possible. To declare the certificate, please make an appointment with the advisor.
Description: The African Studies Program at UW–Madison is one of the world’s leading centers for the study of Africa. Since 1961, the program has been a cornerstone for the study of the continent in the United States and is a federally designated Title VI National Resource Center for Africa. The program brings together faculty and students from across campus and the world to develop and share knowledge about Africa. The undergraduate Certificate in African Studies is a valuable addition to any major. Students in the program gain a deep understanding of the continent’s diverse cultures, histories, languages, and societies. The certificate program is designed to provide students with a multidisciplinary foundation in African studies while allowing them to pursue their own interests within the field. Students can choose from a wide range of courses in departments across the university, including anthropology, art history, geography, history, languages and cultures of Asia and Africa, political science, and sociology.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

Requirements: Undergraduate students in any major may work toward the Certificate in Aging Studies. Students should complete the Certificate Declaration Form. Note: Social Work majors cannot complete the Certificate in Aging Studies. Instead, they can complete the Social Work: Gerontology sub-major.
Description: As the number and proportion of older people in the United States and the world increase, there is a growing need for people who understand the process of aging and who can provide services to an aging population. The certificate in aging studies is an interdisciplinary program that allows students to study the biological, psychological, and sociological aspects of aging, as well as the impact of aging on society. The program is designed to provide students with the knowledge and skills they need to work with older adults in a variety of settings, including healthcare, social services, and government agencies. Students who complete the certificate will be well-prepared for careers in aging-related fields or for graduate study in social work, psychology, sociology, or other disciplines.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://guide.wisc.edu/undergraduate/letters-science/social-work/aging-studies-certificate/

ProgramName: Certificate in American Indian and Indigenous Studies
Requirements: Admission to the certificate is open to any student currently enrolled at UW–Madison as a University Special student. Special students must have a baccalaureate degree from an accredited institution. A student who is interested in the certificate should contact the program advisor to discuss the requirements and to fill out a declaration form.
Description: The American Indian and Indigenous Studies (AIIS) program’s certificate is designed for students who wish to study the history, culture, and contemporary situation of the indigenous peoples of North America and to analyze the relationship between these peoples and the non-indigenous populations. AIIS is a multidisciplinary program, with faculty and courses from various departments throughout the university. The curriculum is designed to provide students with a multifaceted understanding of the diverse histories and cultures of the American Indian and Indigenous peoples of the United States and Canada, as well as their contemporary legal, political, and social status. The certificate is open to all students across the university.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://guide.wisc.edu/nondegree/undergraduate-special-student-certificates/undergraduate-special-student-certificates.pdf

Requirements: All current undergraduate students are eligible to complete the Certificate in Applied Social Research. To declare the certificate, students should contact the Sociology undergraduate advisor.
Description: The Department of Sociology's certificate in applied social research (CASR) is designed to provide students with a strong foundation in the skills used by social scientists to answer questions about the social world. In today’s data-driven world, employers in many fields—including business, government, and the non-profit sector—increasingly seek employees who can understand, conduct, and analyze research. Students who complete the certificate will be well prepared to pursue careers in these fields or to continue their education in graduate school. In the process of completing the certificate, students will: gain a foundation in the logic of social science research; learn how to use a variety of research methods and tools to analyze social data; develop the skills to design and carry out an independent research project; and learn how to communicate research findings to a variety of audiences.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://guide.wisc.edu/undergraduate/letters-science/sociology/applied-social-research-certificate/

ProgramName: Certificate in Arabic Language and Culture
Requirements: Students may declare the certificate at any time by meeting with the advisor.
Description: Students will study the Arabic language as they learn about the literature and culture of the Arabic-speaking world. This certificate is open to all students and is especially valuable to students majoring in international studies, business, journalism, political science, and other fields where proficiency in Arabic and an understanding of the culture can be applied. The certificate program consists of five courses for a minimum of 16 credits.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

Requirements: Students should contact the certificate advisor to discuss their interest in the program and to be admitted to the certificate. Declaration of the certificate can happen at any time. To be eligible for the certificate, students must be a currently enrolled undergraduate student at UW–Madison. Students who have already earned an undergraduate degree are not eligible for this certificate.
Description: Archaeology is the study of the human past through its material remains. Archaeologists study the full range of human history, from the first stone tools used by our ancestors millions of years ago to the garbage we produced yesterday. Archaeology allows us to explore the diversity of human experience across time and space, and to understand the processes that have shaped the world we live in today. The Certificate in Archaeology provides students with a broad introduction to the field of archaeology, as well as the opportunity to pursue more specialized interests in particular regions or time periods. Students will learn about the history of the discipline, the theories and methods that archaeologists use to study the past, and the ethical issues that surround the practice of archaeology in the modern world.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://guide.wisc.edu/nondegree/undergraduate-special-student-certificates/undergraduate-special-student-certificates.pdf

Requirements: Students interested in the Certificate in Art History should contact the department's undergraduate advisor. Students should ideally declare the certificate before they have completed more than 9 credits toward the requirements. The Certificate in Art History requires 15 credits in Art History (ART HIST) courses. A minimum 2.000 GPA is required in all certificate courses. At least 9 credits must be completed in residence.
Description: The Certificate in Art History is designed for students who wish to pursue an interest in the history of art and visual culture and can be combined with any undergraduate major. It is especially suited for students in related fields who wish to develop skills in visual analysis, historical and cultural research, and critical writing. The certificate is also popular with students in the humanities and social sciences, the sciences, and those in professional programs like business, nursing, and engineering, who seek a more diverse undergraduate experience.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

Requirements: The Certificate in Art Studio is available to all undergraduate students at UW–Madison who are not majoring in Art or Art Education. To declare the Certificate in Art Studio, students should complete the declaration form on the School of Education website. Students must complete at least 15 credits of ART coursework and earn a minimum 2.000 GPA on all certificate coursework.
Description: The Art Studio certificate is designed for students who want to develop their artistic skills and creative talents. It is intended for students who are not majoring in Art or Art Education, but who have an interest in art and want to take a sequence of courses to develop their skills in a particular area. The certificate is open to all undergraduate students at UW–Madison.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://guide.wisc.edu/undergraduate/education/art/art.pdf
Accredidation: The Art Department is an accredited institutional member of the National Association of Schools of Art and Design (NASAD).

Requirements: Students should contact the certificate advisor to discuss the requirements and declare the certificate.
Description: The Asian American Studies Program (AASP) is an interdisciplinary program within the College of Letters & Science. The program offers an undergraduate certificate that provides students with an opportunity to explore the history, culture, and experiences of Asian Americans in the United States. Through a range of courses in the humanities and social sciences, students will learn to critically analyze the social, political, and economic factors that have shaped the Asian American experience. The program also emphasizes the importance of community engagement and social justice, and provides students with opportunities to connect with Asian American communities in Madison and beyond. Students in the program learn to: demonstrate knowledge of the history, culture, and experiences of Asian Americans; critically analyze the social, political, and economic factors that have shaped the Asian American experience; apply interdisciplinary perspectives to the study of Asian Americans; and engage with Asian American communities and issues through service or research.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

Requirements: To declare the Biocore certificate, students must apply and be accepted into the Biocore program. Students are eligible to apply to Biocore if they have: attained at least sophomore standing (30 credits) by the start of the program; completed the first semester of general chemistry (CHEM 103, CHEM 109, or CHEM 115); and are currently enrolled in or have completed the second semester of general chemistry (CHEM 104, CHEM 109, or CHEM 116).
Description: The Biology Core Curriculum (Biocore) is a four-semester sequence of lecture and laboratory courses, taken in addition to physics and calculus. The curriculum provides a broad, deep, and integrated foundation in biology. Students begin the Biocore sequence as sophomores after completing general chemistry. Biocore’s curriculum provides students with a community of students and faculty who are dedicated to biology research and teaching. This honors-level sequence is designed for students motivated to understand biology at a deep level and is appropriate for students in any biological science major. The program emphasizes scientific reasoning, research, and communication. Students who complete the Biocore curriculum and one additional Biocore course (either a Biocore lab or the Biocore capstone) fulfill the requirements for the Biocore certificate.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

Requirements: To declare the Certificate in Business, students must meet the following requirements: Have a minimum 2.750 cumulative GPA at UW–Madison; Have completed at least 12 credits in residence at UW–Madison. Business students are not eligible to complete the Certificate in Business.
Description: The Certificate in Business (CPB) is designed for students who are not majoring in business but want to gain a foundation in the core concepts of business. The program provides students with the tools to understand the business environment and how to apply business principles in their chosen career path. Students will learn the fundamentals of accounting, finance, management, and marketing.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://guide.wisc.edu/undergraduate/business/school-wide/business-certificate/business-certificate.pdf

ProgramName: Certificate in Chicanx and Latinx Studies
Requirements: Students may declare the Chicanx and Latinx Studies Certificate at any time. Declaration consists of a meeting with the CLS advisor to discuss interest in the certificate and to develop a plan for completion of the requirements. To set up a meeting, students should use the scheduling tool Starfish or email the advisor.
Description: Chicanx and Latinx studies (CLS) is a multidisciplinary field of study that examines the historical and contemporary experiences of people of Mexican, Caribbean, Central American, and South American heritage in the United States. The Chicanx and Latinx studies certificate program is designed for students who wish to explore these experiences while pursuing a major in another department or college. Drawing on the expertise of its faculty in the social sciences, humanities, and the arts, CLS offers students a wide range of courses and a focus on three areas: historical and contemporary experiences; language and literature; and health and social issues. The certificate program provides a valuable foundation for students planning careers in education, law, medicine, social work, business, journalism, and government, as well as for those pursuing graduate study in the humanities and social sciences.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

Requirements: The Certificate in Classical Studies is open to all students at UW–Madison. To declare the certificate, students should contact the undergraduate advisor. Students must maintain a minimum 2.000 GPA in all certificate coursework, and at least 9 credits must be earned in residence.
Description: The undergraduate certificate in Classical Studies provides students with a broad and flexible introduction to the history, literature, and culture of the ancient Mediterranean world. Classical studies is inherently interdisciplinary, including the study of languages, literature, history, art, architecture, philosophy, and religion. Students can choose to focus their certificate on one of these areas or take a broad range of courses across the curriculum. The certificate is open to all undergraduates.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

Requirements: Students who wish to declare the certificate in computer sciences should go to the Computer Sciences department website for the declaration form and instructions. To be eligible to declare the Computer Sciences certificate, students must: 1. Be a degree-seeking undergraduate student at UW–Madison. 2. Not be a Computer Sciences major. 3. Have completed COMP SCI 300 Programming II or COMP SCI 220 Data Science Programming I. 4. Earn a grade of C or better in that course.
Description: The Computer Sciences Department is one of the oldest and top-ranked CS departments in the world. The department offers a certificate in computer sciences for students who are not majoring in computer sciences but who wish to supplement their major with a foundation in computer sciences. The certificate provides students with a strong background in the field, including programming, data structures, and a choice of several upper-level courses.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://guide.wisc.edu/undergraduate/letters-science/computer-sciences/computer-sciences-certificate/computer-sciences-certificate.pdf

Requirements: All undergraduate students at UW–Madison are eligible to apply for the Criminal Justice Certificate. Students are encouraged to declare the certificate as early as possible so they can plan their course of study and receive program updates. To declare the Criminal Justice Certificate, students must meet with the criminal justice advisor.
Description: The Center for Law, Society & Justice administers the Certificate in Criminal Justice. The Criminal Justice Certificate provides students with a multidisciplinary framework for understanding the causes and consequences of crime, the structure and function of the criminal legal system, and the nature of social control and justice. Students learn to think critically about how legal and social institutions interact to shape human behavior and social life. The program is designed to be a useful addition to the programs of students who plan to go into law, law enforcement, social work, or other justice-related professions, and for students who are interested in the criminal legal system.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://guide.wisc.edu/undergraduate/letters-science/center-law-society-justice/criminal-justice-certificate/criminal-justice-certificate.pdf

Requirements: Students interested in the Certificate in Dance must meet with the Dance Department undergraduate advisor to discuss the requirements and declare the certificate.
Description: The Certificate in Dance is for students who wish to pursue an interest in dance while majoring in another field. The certificate is designed for students to develop skills and knowledge in dance as an art form through technical training, creative practice, and theoretical study. Students in the certificate program represent many areas of study across the UW–Madison campus, and they find that dance provides a complementary perspective to their other academic and professional interests.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://guide.wisc.edu/undergraduate/undergraduate.pdf
Accredidation: The dance department is an accredited institutional member of the National Association of Schools of Dance (NASD).

Requirements: To declare the Certificate in Data Science, a student must: be a declared undergraduate student at UW–Madison; have completed MATH 221, MATH 171, or MATH 211; have a 2.000 GPA or higher. Students should contact the Statistics Department or a Data Science advisor to discuss the certificate and declare.
Description: The Certificate in Data Science is a program designed for students wanting to gain additional skills in data science to help in their future careers. In today's digital age, data is being collected in almost every field of study. Data science is the field that brings together statistics, mathematics, and computer science to help make sense of all that data. The certificate is intended for students who want to develop their ability to solve problems by utilizing data. The certificate consists of 5 courses (13-16 credits) across four areas: Statistics, Computer Science, Data Ethics, and a capstone course. Students will learn how to approach a problem using data, how to manage and visualize data, and how to use data to make predictions.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

Requirements: Undergraduate students from any school or college at UW–Madison may declare the Design Strategy Certificate. Students should consult with the certificate advisor to discuss their interest in the certificate and to declare the program.
Description: The Certificate in Design Strategy provides a design thinking foundation for students in any major across the university. The program introduces students to the fundamentals of design, design thinking, and strategic design—allowing students to hone their problem-solving and critical thinking skills. This certificate is designed for students wanting to add a creative and innovative perspective to their undergraduate major. Students from any major are encouraged to complete the certificate. Students in the certificate program will learn how to apply a design thinking process to identify and solve problems. They will be able to apply creative and strategic design skills to their primary field of study. The curriculum provides a background in design fundamentals and then moves through a sequence of courses that emphasize the design process, from research and ideation to implementation and evaluation.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://guide.wisc.edu/undergraduate/human-ecology/design-studies/design-strategy-certificate/

Requirements: The Digital Media Analytics certificate is available to any student who is currently enrolled in a degree-seeking program at UW–Madison. Students should meet with the certificate advisor to discuss their interest in the program and how the certificate requirements fit into their overall graduation plan. Students should complete or be currently enrolled in JOURN 202 Mass Communication Practices before declaring the certificate.
Department: School of Journalism and Mass Communication
Description: The School of Journalism and Mass Communication (SJMC) offers a Certificate in Digital Media Analytics (DMA). Digital media have transformed the field of communication, as well as the world around us. In this environment, the ability to find, analyze, and interpret data has become a critical skill for any communication professional. The Certificate in Digital Media Analytics is designed to provide students with the skills and knowledge they need to understand and use data in a variety of communication contexts. Through a combination of coursework and hands-on experience, students will learn how to use data to inform communication strategies, evaluate the effectiveness of digital media campaigns, and understand how digital media is changing the way we communicate.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://guide.wisc.edu/undergraduate/letters-science/journalism-mass-communication/digital-media-analytics-certificate/digital-media-analytics-certificate_howtogetintext.pdf

Requirements: To declare the Certificate in Digital Studies, students must have completed at least one course toward the certificate. Students may declare the certificate by filling out the online declaration form on the program website. The declaration form includes short-answer questions, including an explanation of how the certificate fits into the student's academic or career goals.
Description: Digital technology has changed the way we think, the way we create, and the way we communicate. It impacts our work, our play, and our world. The undergraduate Certificate in Digital Studies is an interdisciplinary program that allows students to explore these changes. Students will choose from a wide range of courses to build a curriculum that meets their needs and interests. The certificate is designed for students who want to develop their digital skills and their understanding of the digital world. By choosing courses from several departments, students can build a program of study that is both broad and deep. The certificate is open to all undergraduate students at UW–Madison.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

Requirements: To declare the East Asian Studies Certificate, students should contact the advisor. Students may declare the certificate at any time.
Description: The Center for East Asian Studies (CEAS) provides a focal point for the study of East Asia (China, Japan, Korea, and Tibet/Central Asia) at the University of Wisconsin–Madison. CEAS is part of the Institute for Regional and International Studies (IRIS), which is a center within the International Division. The East Asian Studies certificate provides students with an interdisciplinary program of study that combines a focus on the language(s) of the region with coursework in one or more other disciplines (e.g., anthropology, art history, history, religious studies, political science, and sociology). Students may also include courses in literature and linguistics.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://guide.wisc.edu/undergraduate/letters-science/institute-regional-international-studies/east-asian-studies-certificate/
ScholarshipType: Fellowships, Foreign Language and Area Studies (FLAS) Fellowships

Requirements: Students may declare the Certificate in Economics at any time. To declare the certificate, students must have: Completed ECON 101 or ECON 111 with a grade of C or better; Completed ECON 102 or ECON 110 with a grade of C or better; Completed MATH 211, MATH 217, or MATH 221 with a grade of C or better. Students declare the certificate by completing the online declaration form on the Department of Economics website.
Description: Economics is the study of how people, organizations, and societies make choices about the use of resources. It is a social science that uses mathematical models and statistical methods to understand how markets work and how public policy can influence economic outcomes. Students who study economics learn how to think critically, solve problems, and communicate complex ideas. These skills are highly valued by employers in a wide range of industries, including finance, consulting, government, and non-profit organizations. The Certificate in Economics is designed for students who want to gain a strong foundation in economic theory and its applications. It is a flexible program that allows students to choose from a variety of elective courses that match their interests and career goals. The certificate is open to all undergraduate students at UW–Madison, except for those who are majoring in economics.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

ProgramName: Certificate in Education and Educational Services
Requirements: Declaration of the Certificate in Education and Educational Services is open to any student who has completed at least 30 undergraduate credits. To declare the certificate, please complete the online declaration form found on the School of Education website.
Description: The Certificate in Education and Educational Services (CEES) provides students with a cohesive set of courses that focus on the psychology of learning and the role of education in society. The CEES is intended for students who are interested in the field of education but are not seeking teacher certification. The CEES provides a foundation for students who are interested in pursuing a career in an education-related field, such as educational research, policy, or community-based educational programming. The CEES is also appropriate for students who are interested in pursuing a graduate degree in education or a related field.

It is meant to be a flexible, value-added program that can be completed alongside any major at UW-Madison. To ensure a well-rounded and interdisciplinary experience, students take coursework in natural sciences, social sciences, and humanities, and complete a final capstone project. By blending their major degree with the environmental studies certificate, students gain a unique perspective on environmental issues that will serve them well in any career path.

Requirements: Undergraduate students may declare the certificate at any time. To declare, students should contact the Folklore Program director or advisor.
Description: Folklore is the study of the traditional, vernacular, and expressive cultures of groups—ethnic, religious, regional, occupational, and familial. Folklorists focus on the study of informal, face-to-face, or small-group communications and artistic expressions within those groups. They seek to understand the significance of songs, stories, rituals, and material culture in everyday life. Students of folklore explore how the past influences the present and how groups use traditional culture to communicate, resist, or accommodate within the context of global, national, and local forces. The Folklore Program offers an undergraduate certificate in folklore for students with an interest in vernacular and traditional culture. It is designed for students with majors in any field, from the arts and humanities to the social and natural sciences. The folklore certificate allows students to explore their interests in folklore through a structured, interdisciplinary set of courses. The certificate is an excellent addition to a student’s undergraduate education, providing them with a deeper understanding of the diverse ways in which people communicate and express themselves through tradition. Students will be able to: 1. Define folklore as a discipline and identify its historical and theoretical foundations. 2. Identify and analyze folklore in its various forms (such as song, story, ritual, and material culture) and contexts (such as ethnic, religious, regional, and occupational groups). 3. Understand the relationship between tradition and modernity, and the role of folklore in shaping identity and community. 4. Apply folkloric methods and perspectives to their own lives and fields of study.

Requirements: Students who have reached the level of FRENCH 228 are eligible to declare the French certificate. Students are encouraged to declare as soon as they are eligible. To declare the French certificate, students should contact the undergraduate advisor.
Description: French is one of the world's great languages of culture and diplomacy. It is an official language of the UN, the Red Cross, the International Olympic Committee, and many other international organizations. French is spoken in more than 40 countries and on 5 continents. In our increasingly interconnected world, students who develop a high level of proficiency in French and an understanding of the diverse cultures of the French-speaking world find that their knowledge and skills are relevant to many careers and areas of interest. The French Certificate offers students the opportunity to develop these skills and explore the literatures and cultures of the French-speaking world. A French certificate can be a valuable addition to any major, including those in the sciences, social sciences, business, and the humanities.

Requirements: Students are eligible to declare the Certificate in Game Design after they have completed (or are currently enrolled in) L S 210 Game Design I. To declare the certificate, students should contact the undergraduate advisor for the Department of Communication Arts.
Description: The undergraduate certificate in Game Design provides a foundation for students who want to build, study, and design games. The certificate is a collaboration between the Department of Curriculum & Instruction in the School of Education, the Department of Computer Sciences in the College of Letters & Science, and the Art Department in the School of Education. The Game Design Certificate offers students a coordinated curriculum in the design and study of games, including digital games, card games, and board games. It addresses the needs of a growing number of students across the university who want to pursue careers in the game industry, use games in their own professional practices (e.g., as teachers or health care professionals), or engage in research and scholarship in this area. The certificate consists of a series of core courses and a list of electives that will provide students with the opportunity to pursue their own interests in this field. Students can work on game programming, game art, game design, and/or the study of games as educational tools or cultural artifacts.

ProgramName: Certificate in Gender and Women's Studies
Requirements: Undergraduate students currently enrolled at UW–Madison can declare a certificate in Gender and Women’s Studies. Students are encouraged to declare the certificate early to help with course planning. To declare, students should visit the Gender and Women's Studies website for more information, or meet with the undergraduate advisor.
Description: Gender and Women’s Studies is an interdisciplinary field that offers a critical perspective on how gender—the social meaning of being female or male—and its intersection with other categories of difference such as race, ethnicity, sexual orientation, disability, and class, shape the lives of individuals, as well as the social, cultural, and political structures in which we live. Since gender and women's studies is an interdisciplinary field, our faculty and students utilize a range of different methods and approaches to research and teach about such topics as: the experience of women in different historical periods and in various cultures; the ways in which gender and sexuality are represented in literature and the arts; women's and men's participation in political, social, and economic life; the biology and health of women; the nature of gender and sexual identities; and the value of scientific and social-scientific knowledge about women and gender. Our undergraduate programs prepare students for a wide range of careers in fields such as social services, community organizing, health care, education, law, and business. Our graduates are also well-prepared for advanced study in a variety of graduate and professional programs.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://guide.wisc.edu/undergraduate/letters-science/gender-womens-studies/gender-womens-studies-certificate/

It is influenced by many factors, including the environment, social and economic conditions, and individual behavior. Policy plays a critical role in shaping these factors and influencing health outcomes. The certificate provides students with the skills and knowledge needed to analyze health policy issues and to understand the political, economic, and social contexts in which health policy is made. Students in the certificate will: Explore the factors that influence health and the role of policy in shaping health outcomes; Develop the skills needed to analyze health policy issues; Gain an understanding of the political, economic, and social contexts in which health policy is made.

Description: Material culture is the study of objects—from those of the everyday to the extraordinary—and the way they shape and are shaped by the people who make and use them. Our relationship to the material world is at the core of human history, and we believe that to study things is to better understand ourselves. The Material Culture Program is a collaborative, interdisciplinary community of students and faculty members across the UW–Madison campus who use material things as primary sources for research and as powerful tools for teaching. Our interdisciplinary reach spans numerous departments, representing such diverse fields as Art History, Design Studies, Anthropology, Folklore, Landscape Architecture, Geography, and History. The Certificate in Material Culture program offers students an opportunity to learn how to research and interpret the material world, and provides them with a set of skills that can be applied to many different fields. Students learn about the various ways in which material culture has been studied in the past and how it is being studied today. They also gain hands-on experience in the research, documentation, and interpretation of material objects.

Medieval studies also includes the study of the Byzantine Empire and the Islamic world, as well as the relationships between the Latin West and these other cultures. The certificate is designed for students who want to explore this period from a variety of perspectives, using the resources of several departments. It is an excellent complement to many majors, providing a focus for students' elective courses.

Description: The PEPP certificate is designed to provide students with the opportunity to study the intersection of politics, economics and philosophy. The core of the certificate is a three-course sequence (one in each field) that introduces students to the different ways in which these disciplines approach questions of justice, efficiency and governance. In addition to the core courses, students take three elective courses that allow them to explore specific topics in more depth.

Description: The Certificate in Political Economy, Philosophy, and Politics (PEPP) is designed for students who want to study the intersection of these three disciplines. The program is based on the idea that each of these fields provides a different perspective on the world and that understanding the world requires an appreciation of all three. Political economy studies how people organize themselves to produce and distribute goods and services. Philosophy explores the fundamental questions of human existence, such as the nature of justice, the role of government, and the meaning of life. Politics is the study of how people make decisions together and how power is exercised in society. By studying these three fields together, students will gain a deeper understanding of the complex challenges facing the world today and the different ways that people are trying to address them. The PEPP certificate is open to all students at UW-Madison and is particularly well-suited for students who are interested in pursuing careers in law, public policy, business, or international affairs.

Description: The Certificate in Russian, East European, and Central Asian Studies (REECAS) is designed to give students a multidisciplinary survey of the region. The REECAS region is a vast and diverse area of the world that includes Russia, Eastern and Central Europe, and the Caucasus and Central Asia. The certificate is open to all undergraduates and provides students with the opportunity to explore the history, politics, culture, and languages of this region.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

Requirements: Students who are not already Scandinavian Studies majors are eligible to declare the Certificate in Scandinavian Studies. To declare the certificate, students should contact the undergraduate advisor.
Description: The Department of German, Nordic, and Slavic+ offers several options for the study of Scandinavian (Danish, Finnish, Icelandic, Norwegian, and Swedish) language, literature, and culture. Courses in Scandinavian provide a window into the culture and history of the Nordic countries, and also serve as a tool for understanding the rich and diverse heritage of many people in the Upper Midwest. Many students find that Scandinavian studies is a great addition to their primary major. For example, a student majoring in nursing might want to learn more about the healthcare systems in Scandinavia. A student majoring in political science or international studies may be interested in learning about the Nordic model of social welfare. A student majoring in art history might find inspiration in the work of Edvard Munch or the design of IKEA. No matter what your interests are, the Scandinavian Studies certificate can help you develop a deeper understanding of the world.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

ProgramName: Certificate in Science of Patient Safety
DeadlineDate: Applications are accepted throughout the year
Requirements: All Graduate School students and students in a professional program (Law, Medicine, Nursing, Pharmacy, Veterinary Medicine) may pursue the Science of Patient Safety certificate. Students must have a minimum GPA of 3.0. To apply for the certificate, students should contact the ISyE Graduate Student Services Coordinator.
Description: The Graduate/Professional Certificate in the Science of Patient Safety program is designed for graduate students in the health sciences and engineering and for healthcare professionals. The certificate provides students with the knowledge and skills to apply the concepts and methods of the science of patient safety to their own practice or research. The science of patient safety is an interdisciplinary field that draws on the theories and methods of human factors engineering, health services research, and health care quality improvement. The certificate program is a joint effort of the Department of Industrial and Systems Engineering (ISyE) in the College of Engineering and several health sciences schools (Medicine and Public Health, Nursing, and Pharmacy).

Requirements: All current UW–Madison undergraduates are eligible to complete the South Asian studies certificate. Students interested in declaring the South Asian studies certificate should contact the advisor.
Description: The undergraduate Certificate in South Asian Studies is an interdisciplinary program that allows students to study the diversity and complexity of the South Asian region. South Asia includes the countries of Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan, and Sri Lanka. Students can choose from a range of courses in departments across the university. They explore themes such as religion and philosophy; the arts and literature; history; politics, society, and economics; and the environment. This certificate can be a valuable addition to any major, providing students with a deeper understanding of one of the world's most populous and influential regions.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://guide.wisc.edu/undergraduate/letters-science/institute-regional-international-studies/south-asian-studies-certificate/

Requirements: Students should contact the undergraduate advisor for the Center for Southeast Asian Studies to declare the certificate. Information on the undergraduate advisor can be found on the program website or by contacting the Center for Southeast Asian Studies.
Description: Southeast Asia is a region of diversity, encompassing the nations of Brunei, Cambodia, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia, Myanmar (Burma), the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand, Timor-Leste, and Vietnam. The Certificate in Southeast Asian Studies is designed to provide students with a multidisciplinary grounding in the languages, histories, and cultures of Southeast Asia. It is an excellent way to organize a set of courses around a regional interest, and to have that interest recognized on one’s transcript. The certificate is open to all undergraduate students and is particularly relevant to those planning careers in international business, government, non-governmental organizations, or education. Southeast Asian Studies is a program of the Center for Southeast Asian Studies. The center also offers a major in Southeast Asian Studies through the Department of Asian Languages and Cultures. The Center for Southeast Asian Studies is a Title VI National Resource Center.

Requirements: To declare the Spanish certificate, students must have completed SPANISH 226 or SPANISH 311. Students should then contact a Spanish & Portuguese advisor to declare the certificate.
Description: With more than 400 million speakers, Spanish is the second most spoken language in the world and is the official language of 21 countries. Our Spanish program offers a wealth of courses in the areas of language, literature, culture, and linguistics. This certificate program is for students who want to develop their proficiency in Spanish, as well as their knowledge of the diverse cultures of the Spanish-speaking world.

Requirements: Undergraduate students in good academic standing from any school or college at the University of Wisconsin–Madison are eligible to apply for the Certificate in Sustainability. Students must have at least one semester of coursework remaining to complete the certificate requirements. All students must complete the online application found on the Nelson Institute website. The application consists of a few short-answer questions and a brief meeting with an advisor.
Description: The Sustainability Certificate is for undergraduate students who wish to learn about the environmental, social and economic dimensions of sustainability. This is accomplished through a combination of coursework and a capstone project. The certificate is designed to be flexible and can be completed by students from any major. The certificate is a collaborative effort between the Nelson Institute for Environmental Studies and the Office of Sustainability.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

ProgramName: Certificate in Teaching English to Speakers of Other Languages
Requirements: Applicants must possess a bachelor's degree from an accredited institution. Applicants must have a minimum undergraduate grade point average of 3.00 on a 4.00 scale. Applicants must meet the University of Wisconsin-Madison Graduate School's English proficiency requirements if they are non-native English speakers.
Description: The Certificate in Teaching English to Speakers of Other Languages (TESOL) provides an opportunity for undergraduate students at UW–Madison to develop a basic foundation in linguistics and second language acquisition, to investigate the history and politics of English language teaching, and to explore and apply various methods for teaching English to adult learners in the U.S. and abroad. TESOL certificate students will understand how English is structured and used in various contexts, learn how to design and evaluate instructional materials, and observe and practice teaching English in local contexts. The certificate is open to undergraduate students in any major, and it is a popular credential for students planning to live and work abroad after graduation. The TESOL certificate is not a program that leads to Wisconsin Department of Public Instruction (DPI) teacher certification for K–12 schools.
ProgramWebsiteURL: The official website for the University of Wisconsin–Madison is [wisc.edu](https://www.wisc.edu).

Requirements: All undergraduate students are eligible to apply for the Textiles and Design certificate. Students must have completed 15 credits at UW–Madison and have a cumulative GPA of 2.5 or higher to be eligible for the certificate. Students who meet these requirements should complete the declaration form on the School of Human Ecology website.
Description: The undergraduate certificate in textiles and design is available to all undergraduate students at UW–Madison who are not pursuing the textiles and fashion design major. This certificate allows students to acquire a collection of courses that focuses on the textile and fashion industry as a creative and/or commercial entity. Students choose between a design or business focus.

Requirements: All current UW–Madison undergraduates are eligible to complete the Certificate in Theatre. To declare the certificate, go to the Department of Theatre and Drama website for the current declaration process. Students are encouraged to declare the certificate early in their undergraduate careers to allow for the most flexibility in their schedules.
Description: The certificate in theatre provides students with a broad introduction to the field of theatre and drama and the opportunity to complete work in several areas: acting, stage management, scenic design, costume design, lighting design, theatre technology, and/or theatre history and literature. The certificate can also be used as a way to focus on a specific area of interest. Any undergraduate student may declare the theatre certificate. Most certificate students also choose to participate in university theatre productions in a variety of ways: acting, backstage crew, house management, or design.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://guide.wisc.edu/undergraduate/education/theatre-drama/theatre-certificate/

Requirements: Students must be in good academic standing (GPA 2.0 or higher) to declare the certificate. To declare the certificate, students should contact the certificate advisor. The Visual Culture Certificate is open to all undergraduates at UW–Madison. No prerequisites are required.
Description: The Certificate in Visual Culture provides an opportunity for students to pursue a sustained and focused interest in the history and theory of images and the visual world. It is designed to allow students to choose a set of courses that suits their individual interests and goals from the many visual culture courses offered across the campus. Students are introduced to the fundamental concepts and methods of visual culture through a required core course and develop those interests in greater depth through a 400-level seminar or other advanced course. At the same time, the certificate allows for a maximum of flexibility. Students are encouraged to explore the intersections between visual culture and their primary major, and to build on their own particular interests by choosing from a wide variety of electives. The Certificate in Visual Culture is an interdisciplinary program open to any undergraduate student at the University of Wisconsin–Madison.
